docs.title: go-pki-scep
docs.text:
go-pki-scep is a Go implementation of the Simple Certificate Enrollment Protocol (SCEP, RFC 8894). Routers, VPN gateways, mobile device managers and other network devices use SCEP to request certificates from a CA. The module has three packages:

  • scep builds and parses SCEP messages and answers requests without any transport.
  • scepserver is an http.Handler that serves SCEP for a CA you implement.
  • scepclient enrolls, renews, polls and queries a SCEP server over HTTP.

The library handles the protocol: message signatures and encryption, nonces, transaction IDs, the HTTP operations and the answers. Your code decides who may enroll, issues the certificates and keeps whatever state the CA needs. The CMS layer comes from go-pkcs7. Algorithm choices are made per call through option structs. Nothing is configured through package variables.

go get github.com/misiektoja/go-pki-scep

The module needs Go 1.27.3 or newer. Its only dependency is go-pkcs7.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: go-pki-scep splits SCEP into a message layer and two HTTP packages built on it. The library owns the protocol. The code that embeds it owns authorization, issuance and storage.

docs.title: Packages
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    client["scepclient<br/>HTTP client"] --> scep
    server["scepserver<br/>HTTP handler"] --> scep
    yourca["Your CA<br/>implements scepserver.CA"] --- server
    scep["scep<br/>pkiMessage build, parse, answer"] --> pkcs7["go-pkcs7<br/>SignedData, EnvelopedData"]
    scep --> x509util["x509util<br/>challenge password in CSRs"]
    scep --> cryptoutil["cryptoutil<br/>key identifiers"]
Package Role scep Builds requests, parses and verifies any pkiMessage, decrypts its content and builds the CertRep answers. It has no transport scepserver Serves the SCEP HTTP operations of one URL and passes verified, decrypted requests to a CA you implement scepclient Talks to one SCEP URL: fetches the CA certificates, enrolls, renews, polls, queries and verifies every answer x509util Creates a CSR that carries a challenge password and reads the password back. crypto/x509 cannot add the password cryptoutil Derives the key identifier that scep.CSRTransactionID turns into a transaction ID

internal/testca is the in-memory CA of the tests. It is not part of the API.

docs.title: The pkiMessage
docs.text:
Every PKIOperation request and answer is a pkiMessage: a CMS SignedData whose content is an EnvelopedData, the pkiEnvelope.

Layer Requests CertRep answers Signer The requester. A PKCSReq uses a self-signed certificate for the CSR key, a RenewalReq the certificate being renewed The CA or its RA Signed attributes transactionID, messageType and senderNonce transactionID, messageType, pkiStatus, senderNonce, recipientNonce and, on FAILURE, failInfo pkiEnvelope recipient The CA or RA certificate from GetCACert The certificate that signed the request pkiEnvelope content A CSR, an issuer and subject for CertPoll or an issuer and serial number for GetCert and GetCRL The certificates or the CRL of a SUCCESS answer. PENDING and FAILURE answers carry none

The signature covers the encrypted envelope, so the envelope cannot be swapped without breaking the signature. The recipientNonce of an answer repeats the senderNonce of the request, which ties the answer to one request.

docs.title: A request through the handler
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant D as Device
    participant H as scepserver.Handler
    participant C as Your CA
    D->>H: GetCACaps, GetCACert
    H->>C: CACertificates
    H-->>D: capabilities, CA and RA certificates
    D->>H: PKIOperation with a PKCSReq
    H->>H: verify the signature
    H->>C: Responder for the envelope recipient
    H->>H: decrypt the envelope, check the CSR signature
    H->>C: Enroll
    C-->>H: certificates, ErrPending, *Failure or *Busy
    H-->>D: CertRep signed by the responder

For each PKIOperation the handler:

  1. Reads the message from the POST body or the GET message parameter, within MaxMessageBytes.
  2. Parses it and verifies its signature with the certificate it carries. The signature proves that the requester holds the signer key. A signing-time attribute, when present, must fall within the validity of that certificate.
  3. Refuses a CertRep, which is not a request.
  4. Asks CA.Responder for the identity that the pkiEnvelope is encrypted for.
  5. Refuses with badAlg a request whose signer certificate has no RSA key, because the answer could not be encrypted for it.
  6. Decrypts the pkiEnvelope with the responder key and the accepted ciphers. For an enrollment it checks the CSR signature and reads the challenge password.
  7. Calls Enroll, Poll, GetCert or GetCRL and turns the result into a CertRep, an HTTP 503 or an HTTP 500.

Refusals and logging lists the answer to each failed step.

docs.title: A request through the client
docs.text:
Enroll, Poll, GetCert and GetCRL share one path:

  1. Fetch the capabilities on first use, cache them and pick POST or GET, the digest and the cipher.
  2. Build the request, encrypted for CACertificates.Recipients and signed with the requester certificate.
  3. Send it and retry while the server answers HTTP 503.
  4. Parse the answer and verify its signature against CACertificates.Signers only.
  5. Check that the transaction ID and the recipientNonce match the request.
  6. Decrypt the content of a SUCCESS answer with the requester key.

docs.title: Concurrency
docs.text: A Handler and a Client are safe for concurrent use. The handler calls the CA methods concurrently, so the CA guards its own state. A client caches the capabilities of its server, so one client per server URL serves a whole program.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
This page builds a SCEP server and a client in one Go program and then enrolls against the same server with an independent client. Each part of the program is a place where your own code goes later. The table after the program names the guide page for each one.

The server keeps everything in memory and signs with a throwaway RSA CA that it creates at startup. It issues a certificate for every PKCSReq that carries the challenge password and for every RenewalReq signed with a certificate it issued. It serves plain HTTP on the loopback address. SCEP signs and encrypts each message, so the challenge password does not travel in clear text.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• Go 1.27.3 or newer, the minimum the module declares
  • Port 8080 free on 127.0.0.1 or another address passed with -addr
  • For step 3, certrally or another SCEP client

docs.title: Step 1: create the program
docs.text:
Create a module and add the library:

mkdir scep-quickstart && cd scep-quickstart
go mod init example.com/scep-quickstart
go get github.com/misiektoja/go-pki-scep

The same program is in the repository as examples/quickstart, where go run ./examples/quickstart starts it without any setup. Save it as main.go:

// A local SCEP server for trying go-pki-scep. A throwaway RSA CA checks a challenge password and is
// served over HTTP. A client enrolls and renews against it.
package main

import (
    "bytes"
    "context"
    "crypto/rand"
    "crypto/rsa"
    "crypto/sha256"
    "crypto/subtle"
    "crypto/x509"
    "crypto/x509/pkix"
    "errors"
    "flag"
    "fmt"
    "io"
    "log/slog"
    "math/big"
    "net"
    "net/http"
    "os"
    "os/signal"
    "slices"
    "time"

    scep "github.com/misiektoja/go-pki-scep"
    "github.com/misiektoja/go-pki-scep/scepclient"
    "github.com/misiektoja/go-pki-scep/scepserver"
    "github.com/misiektoja/go-pki-scep/x509util"
)


// quickstartCA issues a certificate for every PKCSReq that carries the challenge password and for
// every RenewalReq signed with a certificate it issued. It keeps nothing on disk.
type quickstartCA struct {
    cert     *x509.Certificate
    key      *rsa.PrivateKey
    password string
}

// newQuickstartCA creates a self-signed RSA CA that lives as long as the process.
func newQuickstartCA(password string) (*quickstartCA, error) {
    key, err := rsa.GenerateKey(rand.Reader, 2048)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    template := &x509.Certificate{
        SerialNumber:          randomSerial(),
        Subject:               pkix.Name{CommonName: "go-pki-scep quickstart CA"},
        NotBefore:             time.Now().Add(-time.Hour),
        NotAfter:              time.Now().Add(30 * 24 * time.Hour),
        IsCA:                  true,
        BasicConstraintsValid: true,
        // The CA key signs CertRep messages and decrypts requests, so it needs both usages.
        KeyUsage: x509.KeyUsageCertSign | x509.KeyUsageCRLSign |
            x509.KeyUsageDigitalSignature | x509.KeyUsageKeyEncipherment,
    }
    der, err := x509.CreateCertificate(rand.Reader, template, template, &key.PublicKey, key)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    cert, err := x509.ParseCertificate(der)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    return &quickstartCA{cert: cert, key: key, password: password}, nil
}

// CACertificates answers GetCACert with the CA certificate for any CA name.
func (ca *quickstartCA) CACertificates(context.Context, string) ([]*x509.Certificate, error) {
    return []*x509.Certificate{ca.cert}, nil
}

// Responder returns the CA identity when the request is encrypted for the CA certificate.
func (ca *quickstartCA) Responder(_ context.Context, recipient scep.IssuerAndSerial) (*scepserver.Responder, error) {
    if !bytes.Equal(recipient.Issuer, ca.cert.RawIssuer) || recipient.SerialNumber.Cmp(ca.cert.SerialNumber) != 0 {
        return nil, scepserver.ErrNotFound
    }
    // The RSA CA key signs the answers and, as a crypto.Decrypter, decrypts the requests.
    return &scepserver.Responder{SignerCertificate: ca.cert, SignerKey: ca.key}, nil
}

// Enroll authorizes a PKCSReq by its challenge password and a RenewalReq by its signer certificate.
func (ca *quickstartCA) Enroll(_ context.Context, req *scepserver.Request) ([]*x509.Certificate, error) {
    msg := req.Message
    switch msg.MessageType {
    case scep.PKCSReq:
        if subtle.ConstantTimeCompare([]byte(msg.ChallengePassword), []byte(ca.password)) != 1 {
            return nil, &scepserver.Failure{Info: scep.BadRequest, Err: errors.New("wrong challenge password")}
        }
    default:
        // A RenewalReq is signed with the certificate being renewed. A real CA also checks that the
        // certificate is not revoked and that the CSR asks for the same subject.
        signer := msg.SignerCertificate
        if err := signer.CheckSignatureFrom(ca.cert); err != nil {
            return nil, &scepserver.Failure{Info: scep.BadRequest, Err: fmt.Errorf("renewal signer: %w", err)}
        }
        // The handler refuses a signing-time outside the certificate validity, but that attribute is
        // optional and set by the signer, so check the current time too.
        if time.Now().After(signer.NotAfter) {
            return nil, &scepserver.Failure{Info: scep.BadRequest, Err: errors.New("renewal signer expired")}
        }
    }
    return ca.issue(msg.CSR)
}

// Poll refuses every CertPoll, because this CA never keeps a request pending.
func (ca *quickstartCA) Poll(context.Context, *scepserver.Request) ([]*x509.Certificate, error) {
    return nil, &scepserver.Failure{Info: scep.BadCertID, Err: errors.New("no pending request")}
}

// issue signs a one-day client certificate for the CSR key and returns it with the CA certificate.
func (ca *quickstartCA) issue(csr *x509.CertificateRequest) ([]*x509.Certificate, error) {
    der, err := x509.CreateCertificate(rand.Reader, &x509.Certificate{
        SerialNumber: randomSerial(),
        Subject:      csr.Subject,
        NotBefore:    time.Now().Add(-time.Minute),
        NotAfter:     time.Now().Add(24 * time.Hour),
        KeyUsage:     x509.KeyUsageDigitalSignature | x509.KeyUsageKeyEncipherment,
        ExtKeyUsage:  []x509.ExtKeyUsage{x509.ExtKeyUsageClientAuth},
    }, ca.cert, csr.PublicKey, ca.key)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    cert, err := x509.ParseCertificate(der)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    return []*x509.Certificate{cert, ca.cert}, nil
}


// randomSerial returns a random 64-bit certificate serial number.
func randomSerial() *big.Int {
    serial, err := rand.Int(rand.Reader, new(big.Int).Lsh(big.NewInt(1), 64))
    if err != nil {
        panic(err)
    }
    return serial
}

// server is the running SCEP server.
type server struct {
    url         string
    fingerprint [32]byte
    http        *http.Server
}

// start serves SCEP for a new CA on addr under the path /scep.
func start(ctx context.Context, addr, password string, logs io.Writer) (*server, error) {
    ca, err := newQuickstartCA(password)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    handler, err := scepserver.NewHandler(ca, scepserver.Options{
        Logger: slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(logs, nil)),
    })
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    mux := http.NewServeMux()
    mux.Handle("/scep", handler)
    listener, err := (&net.ListenConfig{}).Listen(ctx, "tcp", addr)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    srv := &server{
        url:         "http://" + listener.Addr().String() + "/scep",
        fingerprint: sha256.Sum256(ca.cert.Raw),
        http:        &http.Server{Handler: mux, ReadHeaderTimeout: 10 * time.Second},
    }
    go func() { _ = srv.http.Serve(listener) }()
    return srv, nil
}

// close stops the server.
func (s *server) close() {
    ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
    defer cancel()
    _ = s.http.Shutdown(ctx)
}


// enrollAndRenew enrolls a new key with a PKCSReq and renews its certificate with a RenewalReq.
func enrollAndRenew(ctx context.Context, serverURL string, caFingerprint [32]byte, password string, out io.Writer) error {
    ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, time.Minute)
    defer cancel()
    client, err := scepclient.New(serverURL, scepclient.Options{})
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    ca, err := client.GetCACert(ctx)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    if err := checkCACertificates(ca, caFingerprint); err != nil {
        return err
    }
    cert, key, err := enroll(ctx, client, ca, password)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    _, _ = fmt.Fprintf(out, "Enrolled %s with serial %s\n", cert.Subject, cert.SerialNumber)
    renewed, err := renew(ctx, client, ca, cert, key)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    _, _ = fmt.Fprintf(out, "Renewed %s with serial %s\n", renewed.Subject, renewed.SerialNumber)
    return nil
}



// checkCACertificates trusts a GetCACert answer only when the CA certificate has the fingerprint
// obtained out of band and every certificate that signs or decrypts for it was issued by that CA.
func checkCACertificates(ca *scepclient.CACertificates, fingerprint [32]byte) error {
    if sha256.Sum256(ca.CA.Raw) != fingerprint {
        return errors.New("the CA certificate does not match the pinned fingerprint")
    }
    for _, cert := range slices.Concat(ca.Signers, ca.Recipients) {
        if cert.Equal(ca.CA) {
            continue
        }
        if err := cert.CheckSignatureFrom(ca.CA); err != nil {
            return fmt.Errorf("RA certificate %s: %w", cert.Subject, err)
        }
    }
    return nil
}



// enroll creates an RSA key and a CSR with the challenge password and enrolls it with a PKCSReq.
func enroll(ctx context.Context, client *scepclient.Client, ca *scepclient.CACertificates, password string) (*x509.Certificate, *rsa.PrivateKey, error) {
    key, err := rsa.GenerateKey(rand.Reader, 2048)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, nil, err
    }
    der, err := x509util.CreateCertificateRequest(rand.Reader, &x509util.CertificateRequest{
        Subject:           pkix.Name{CommonName: "quickstart-device"},
        ChallengePassword: password,
    }, key)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, nil, err
    }
    csr, err := x509.ParseCertificateRequest(der)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, nil, err
    }
    // A PKCSReq is signed with a self-signed certificate for the CSR key. The answer is encrypted
    // for that certificate.
    signer, err := selfSigned(key, csr.Subject)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, nil, err
    }
    res, err := client.EnrollAndWait(ctx, ca, scepclient.EnrollRequest{
        CSR:               csr,
        SignerCertificate: signer,
        SignerKey:         key,
    }, 5*time.Second)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, nil, err
    }
    if res.Status != scep.SUCCESS {
        return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("enrollment answered %s %s", res.Status, res.FailInfo)
    }
    return res.Certificate, key, nil
}

// selfSigned returns a short-lived self-signed certificate for key.
func selfSigned(key *rsa.PrivateKey, subject pkix.Name) (*x509.Certificate, error) {
    template := &x509.Certificate{
        SerialNumber: randomSerial(),
        Subject:      subject,
        NotBefore:    time.Now().Add(-time.Hour),
        NotAfter:     time.Now().Add(time.Hour),
        KeyUsage:     x509.KeyUsageDigitalSignature | x509.KeyUsageKeyEncipherment,
    }
    der, err := x509.CreateCertificate(rand.Reader, template, template, &key.PublicKey, key)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    return x509.ParseCertificate(der)
}



// renew requests a certificate for a new key with a RenewalReq signed by the current certificate.
func renew(ctx context.Context, client *scepclient.Client, ca *scepclient.CACertificates, cert *x509.Certificate, key *rsa.PrivateKey) (*x509.Certificate, error) {
    newKey, err := rsa.GenerateKey(rand.Reader, 2048)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    der, err := x509.CreateCertificateRequest(rand.Reader, &x509.CertificateRequest{Subject: cert.Subject}, newKey)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    csr, err := x509.ParseCertificateRequest(der)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    res, err := client.Enroll(ctx, ca, scepclient.EnrollRequest{
        MessageType:       scep.RenewalReq,
        CSR:               csr,
        SignerCertificate: cert,
        SignerKey:         key,
    })
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    if res.Status != scep.SUCCESS {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("renewal answered %s %s", res.Status, res.FailInfo)
    }
    return res.Certificate, nil
}


// run serves SCEP on addr, enrolls and renews once with the client and serves until ctx ends.
func run(ctx context.Context, addr, password string, out io.Writer) error {
    srv, err := start(ctx, addr, password, os.Stderr)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    defer srv.close()
    if err := enrollAndRenew(ctx, srv.url, srv.fingerprint, password, out); err != nil {
        return err
    }
    _, _ = fmt.Fprintf(out, "Serving %s with the challenge password %q.\n", srv.url, password)
    _, _ = fmt.Fprintf(out, "CA certificate SHA-256 fingerprint: %x\n", srv.fingerprint)
    _, _ = fmt.Fprintln(out, "Press Ctrl+C to stop.")
    <-ctx.Done()
    return nil
}

// main parses the flags and runs the server until it is interrupted.
func main() {
    addr := flag.String("addr", "127.0.0.1:8080", "address to serve SCEP on")
    password := flag.String("challenge", "secret", "challenge password a PKCSReq must carry")
    flag.Parse()
    ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt)
    err := run(ctx, *addr, *password, os.Stdout)
    stop()
    if err != nil {
        _, _ = fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "quickstart:", err)
        os.Exit(1)
    }
}

Record the packages it imports in go.mod:

Part What the quickstart does What replaces it quickstartCA.Enroll Compares the challenge password with one fixed value and accepts a RenewalReq signed with any certificate it issued Your authorization policy, see Implementing a CA quickstartCA.issue Signs a one-day client certificate with an in-memory key Your CA and its certificate profiles quickstartCA.Responder Signs answers and decrypts requests with the CA key The CA key or an RA, see Implementing a CA quickstartCA.Poll Refuses every CertPoll, because nothing is ever pending A store of pending requests, see Pending requests and throttling checkCACertificates Pins a fingerprint the program knows because it created the CA A fingerprint distributed out of band, see CA certificates and trust enroll and renew Enroll a new RSA key and renew its certificate The device side, see Enrollment and renewal

docs.title: Step 2: run it
docs.text:
go run .

The program enrolls and renews once with the client, prints the server URL and the fingerprint of the CA certificate and keeps serving until you press Ctrl+C:

Enrolled CN=quickstart-device with serial 17480416376858012702
Renewed CN=quickstart-device with serial 17122936644825487411
Serving http://127.0.0.1:8080/scep with the challenge password "secret".
CA certificate SHA-256 fingerprint: 9d46bf304ffba20208369bc0279776c6a97d06bc95b368abc42a8a165b4c22cb
Press Ctrl+C to stop.

The handler logs every PKIOperation answer to standard error:

time=2026-11-03T15:06:53.661+01:00 level=INFO msg="scep request answered" message_type="PKCSReq (19)" transaction_id=b181e23f076b96349c0f9a7f5a2bd48c9166d0c0 status="SUCCESS (0)"
time=2026-11-03T15:06:53.717+01:00 level=INFO msg="scep request answered" message_type="RenewalReq (17)" transaction_id=5cf166dc4765384224c6a14442b5beef4ed759ea status="SUCCESS (0)"

The serial numbers, the transaction IDs and the fingerprint change on every run, because the CA and the keys are created at startup. Ask the server for its capabilities:

curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/scep?operation=GetCACaps'

AES
DES3
POSTPKIOperation
Renewal
SCEPStandard
SHA-1
SHA-256
SHA-512

Server options explains how the handler derives this list.

docs.title: Step 3: enroll with another client
docs.text:
Leave the server running. In a second terminal, enroll with certrally. Replace FINGERPRINT with the fingerprint the server printed, so certrally refuses any other CA certificate:

certrally scep enroll --server http://127.0.0.1:8080/scep --fingerprint FINGERPRINT --challenge secret --subject CN=device-1 --cert-out device.pem --key-out device.key

Renew the certificate with a RenewalReq signed by it:

certrally scep renew --server http://127.0.0.1:8080/scep --fingerprint FINGERPRINT --cert device.pem --key device.key --cert-out device-new.pem --key-out device-new.key

A request with another challenge password gets a FAILURE answer with badRequest. The server log shows the cause, which is not sent to the client:

time=2026-11-03T15:06:54.157+01:00 level=INFO msg="scep request answered" message_type="PKCSReq (19)" transaction_id=B485DB38004DF987172810E833FB1BB48D72867B status="FAILURE (2)" fail_info="badRequest (2)" cause="wrong challenge password"

With --key-type ecdsa-p256 certrally signs the request with a separate RSA key, because the answer is encrypted for the certificate that signed the request. The CA still issues the certificate for the ECDSA key in the CSR. These commands were checked by hand with certrally v0.4.2. CI does not run them.

docs.title: Before production
docs.text:
The quickstart leaves out what a real CA needs:

  • Authorization. One fixed challenge password lets anyone who knows it enroll any subject. Issue one-time passwords per device and check the requested subject. Check that the certificate that signs a RenewalReq is not revoked.
  • Keys. The CA key lives in memory. Keep it in your CA or an HSM. Responder.SignerKey is a crypto.Signer and Responder.DecrypterKey a crypto.Decrypter, so neither has to leave the device that holds it.
  • Trust distribution. Devices need the CA fingerprint before their first request, through provisioning or an MDM profile.
  • Limits. The handler does not rate limit clients. Put middleware in front of it, as Security model describes.

docs.title: RSA keys for encryption
docs.text:
Requests are encrypted for an RSA CA or RA certificate and answers for the request signer certificate, both with RSA key transport. A device must therefore sign its requests with an RSA key. A CA with an ECDSA or Ed25519 key needs an RSA RA certificate to receive requests. The handler answers a request signed with another key type with badAlg and the cause ErrSignerNotRSA. The client returns ErrNoRSARecipient when the CA certificates hold no RSA certificate.

SCEP can also encrypt answers for a non-RSA requester with the challenge password through PasswordRecipientInfo. go-pki-scep does not support that. A CSR may still carry an ECDSA key when an RSA certificate signs the request.

docs.title: No storage
docs.text: The library keeps no state between requests. The CA implementation keeps pending requests, issued certificates, revocation state and CRLs.

docs.title: No trust decisions in the client
docs.text: The client does not validate the GetCACert answer against any trust anchor. The caller decides whether to trust it, for example by a pinned fingerprint, as CA certificates and trust shows.

docs.title: No automatic CA rollover
docs.text: GetNextCACert returns the next CA certificates. The caller stores them and switches to them.

docs.title: Algorithms
docs.text:
• No AES-GCM content encryption and no AuthEnvelopedData.
  • Answers from the handler always use RSA PKCS #1 v1.5 key transport, even for a request that used RSAES-OAEP.

docs.title: Client
docs.text:
• Enroll sends PKCSReq and RenewalReq. An UpdateReq needs the message layer.
  • Retry-After is read in seconds. HTTP dates are ignored and the delay is capped at five minutes.

docs.title: Server
docs.text:
• No rate limiting per client. Put middleware in front of the handler.
  • The handler does not check a capability list set through Options.Capabilities against what it supports.

docs.title: Message layer
docs.text:
The scep package builds, parses and answers pkiMessages without any transport. scepserver and scepclient use it. So can code with another HTTP stack, tools that inspect captured messages and tests that need SCEP messages.

The steps below are taken from Example in the package documentation, which the tests run. It builds a PKCSReq, answers it as a CA and reads the answer as the requester.

docs.title: Building a request
docs.text:
req, err := scep.NewCSRRequest(scep.PKCSReq, csr, scep.RequestOptions{
    Recipients:        []*x509.Certificate{caCert},
    SignerCertificate: deviceCert,
    SignerKey:         deviceKey,
})
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
Function Message Content NewCSRRequest PKCSReq, RenewalReq or UpdateReq The CSR NewCertPollRequest CertPoll The DER encoded CA name and CSR subject. RequestOptions.TransactionID must name the enrollment NewGetCertRequest GetCert The DER encoded issuer name and the serial number NewGetCRLRequest GetCRL The DER encoded issuer name and the serial number

RequestOptions sets what every request needs:

Field Meaning Default Recipients The CA or RA certificates the pkiEnvelope is encrypted for Required SignerCertificate, SignerKey The certificate and key that sign the request Required TransactionID The transaction ID Derived from the CSR key by NewCSRRequest. Required by NewCertPollRequest. Random for NewGetCertRequest and NewGetCRLRequest Digest The signature digest SHA-256 Encryption The content cipher, key transport and OAEP hash AES-128-CBC with RSA PKCS #1 v1.5

The built message has Raw, the DER encoded pkiMessage to send. Its SenderNonce is the nonce an answer must repeat.

docs.title: Answering a request
docs.text:
msg, err := scep.ParsePKIMessage(req.Raw, scep.ParseOptions{})
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
if err := msg.DecryptPKIEnvelope(caCert, caKey, pkcs7.DecryptOptions{}); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
opts := scep.ResponseOptions{SignerCertificate: caCert, SignerKey: caKey}
var rep *scep.PKIMessage
if msg.ChallengePassword != "secret" {
    rep, err = msg.Fail(scep.BadRequest, opts)
} else {
    rep, err = msg.Success([]*x509.Certificate{issueExample(caCert, caKey, msg.CSR), caCert}, opts)
}
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

ParsePKIMessage reads DER or BER and verifies the signature. The message must have exactly one signer. Without ParseOptions.Signers, the signature is checked with the certificate the message carries, which proves only that the sender holds that key. Authorize the sender separately, by the challenge password of a PKCSReq or the signer certificate of a RenewalReq.

DecryptPKIEnvelope decrypts the content with an RSA key and parses it by message type:

Message Field set after decryption PKCSReq, RenewalReq, UpdateReq CSR, ChallengePassword and RawDecrypted through the embedded *CSRReqMessage. The CSR signature is checked CertPoll PollRequest with the issuer and subject GetCert, GetCRL CertificateID with the issuer and serial number CertRep with SUCCESS CertRepMessage.Certificates or CRL

EnvelopeRecipients lists the issuer and serial number of each recipient before decryption, so a server with several keys can pick the one to decrypt with.

An answer is built from the parsed request:

Method Answers Content Success Enrollments, CertPoll and GetCert The certificates, the issued or requested one first SuccessCRL GetCRL The DER encoded CRL Pending Enrollments and CertPoll None Fail Any request None. The failInfo must be one RFC 8894 defines

ResponseOptions names the signer and the algorithms:

Field Meaning Default SignerCertificate, SignerKey The CA or RA certificate and key that sign the answer Required Certificates Certificates carried next to the signer certificate, such as the CA certificate when an RA signs None Digest The signature digest The request digest when it is MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512, otherwise SHA-256 ContentEncryption The cipher of the encrypted content The request cipher. AES-128-CBC when the request was not decrypted

The content of a SUCCESS answer is encrypted for the certificate that signed the request, with RSA PKCS #1 v1.5 key transport.

docs.title: Reading an answer
docs.text:
answer, err := scep.ParsePKIMessage(rep.Raw, scep.ParseOptions{Signers: []*x509.Certificate{caCert}})
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
if err := answer.MatchesRequest(req); err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
if answer.PKIStatus == scep.SUCCESS {
    if err := answer.DecryptPKIEnvelope(deviceCert, deviceKey, pkcs7.DecryptOptions{}); err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }
    fmt.Println(answer.PKIStatus, answer.CertRepMessage.Certificates[0].Subject)
}

A requester sets ParseOptions.Signers to the CA and RA certificates it trusts. Only those certificates take part in the signature check, so a certificate the answer carries cannot stand in for them. An answer that carries no certificates still verifies. MatchesRequest checks that the transactionID matches and that the recipientNonce repeats the senderNonce of the request.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• PKIMessage embeds *CertRepMessage and *CSRReqMessage, so their fields are promoted. Reading msg.PKIStatus on a message that is not a CertRep or msg.CSR before decryption dereferences a nil pointer and panics. Check MessageType first.
  • msg.Certificates holds the certificates the SignedData carries. The certificates of a SUCCESS answer are msg.CertRepMessage.Certificates.
  • MD5 signatures are refused unless ParseOptions.AllowMD5 is set.
  • ParseOptions.LegacyCertificateParser accepts certificates that mark the authority key identifier critical, which some Windows SCEP clients send.

docs.title: Other helpers
docs.text: Function Purpose CSRTransactionID The transaction ID NewCSRRequest derives from a CSR key, so a requester can poll without storing it DegenerateCertificates Encodes certificates as a certificate-only SignedData, the body of a GetCACert answer with several certificates CACerts Reads the certificates of a certificate-only SignedData SignedCertificates Builds a GetNextCACert answer signed by the current CA or RA ParseSignedCertificates Verifies a GetNextCACert answer against the current certificates and returns the announced ones FingerprintCertsSelector, EnciphermentCertsSelector, NopCertsSelector Filter certificates by fingerprint or by key usage. NopCertsSelector passes them through unchanged

docs.title: Support matrix
docs.text: What the handler, the client and the message layer support. Known limitations lists what they do not.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
Operation Server handler Client GetCACaps Lists the capabilities derived from the options and the CA. Options.Capabilities replaces the list GetCACaps, fetched once and used to pick POST, the digest and the cipher GetCACert One DER certificate. The CA and RA certificates in a certificate-only message when there are several GetCACert, which sorts the answer into the CA, the encryption recipients and the allowed CertRep signers GetNextCACert The next CA certificates, signed by the current CA or RA, when the CA implements NextCAGetter GetNextCACert, which verifies the signature against the current certificates GetCACertChain The CA certificate and its issuers up to the root, when the CA implements ChainGetter GetCACertChain, which returns the chain in server order PKIOperation GET with a base64 message parameter and POST with a binary body POST when the server lists POSTPKIOperation or SCEPStandard, GET otherwise

GetCACertChain is not part of RFC 8894. Some CAs serve it and their clients still send it. Its answer carries no RA certificates, so a client enrolls with the GetCACert answer.

docs.title: Message types
docs.text:
Message type Built with Client Handler passes it to Possible answers PKCSReq (19) NewCSRRequest Enroll, EnrollAndWait CA.Enroll SUCCESS, PENDING, FAILURE RenewalReq (17) NewCSRRequest Enroll with MessageType: scep.RenewalReq CA.Enroll SUCCESS, PENDING, FAILURE UpdateReq (18) NewCSRRequest Not sent CA.Enroll SUCCESS, PENDING, FAILURE CertPoll (20) NewCertPollRequest Poll, EnrollAndWait CA.Poll SUCCESS, PENDING, FAILURE GetCert (21) NewGetCertRequest GetCert CertificateGetter.GetCert SUCCESS with certificates, FAILURE GetCRL (22) NewGetCRLRequest GetCRL CRLGetter.GetCRL SUCCESS with a CRL, FAILURE CertRep (3) Success, SuccessCRL, Pending, Fail Parsed and matched to the request Refused with HTTP 400 None

UpdateReq comes from SCEP drafts before RFC 8894. The handler and the message layer treat it like a RenewalReq.

docs.title: Algorithms
docs.text: Area Supported Default Signature digest SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA-224, SHA-1 and MD5 SHA-256. The client picks SHA-256 when the server lists SHA-256 or SCEPStandard, then SHA-512, then SHA-1 MD5 signatures The handler accepts them with Options.AllowMD5, the client only in the answer to a request it signed with MD5 and the message layer with ParseOptions.AllowMD5 Refused Answer digest Any of the above The request digest when it is MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512, otherwise SHA-256 Content cipher AES-128-CBC, AES-192-CBC, AES-256-CBC, DES-EDE3-CBC and DES-CBC AES-128-CBC. The client picks DES-EDE3-CBC when the server lists DES3 without AES or SCEPStandard Accepted on decryption AES-CBC and DES-EDE3-CBC. DES-CBC only when Decrypt lists it. The client always accepts the cipher of its own request Answer cipher Any of the above The request cipher Request key transport RSA PKCS #1 v1.5 and RSAES-OAEP through Encryption.KeyEncryption PKCS #1 v1.5 Answer key transport RSA PKCS #1 v1.5

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
Key Supported types Request signer, which also decrypts the answer RSA. The handler answers any other key with badAlg CSR key Any key crypto/x509 parses and whose CSR signature it checks. x509util.CreateCertificateRequest adds a challenge password for RSA and ECDSA keys Request recipient, the CA or RA certificate that decrypts requests RSA Answer signer, the CA or RA certificate that signs CertRep messages RSA or ECDSA

A device with an ECDSA key signs its PKCSReq with a separate RSA key and certificate. The CSR keeps the ECDSA key and the CA issues the certificate for it. A CA with an ECDSA key needs an RSA RA certificate to decrypt requests.

docs.title: Go and platforms
docs.text: The module needs Go 1.27.3 or newer. CI tests every change on Linux and macOS with the Go version in go.mod and builds it on Windows.

docs.title: Interoperability
docs.text: The Interop workflow runs sscep v0.10.0 and the micromdm/scep v2.3.0 client against the handler, and the client against the micromdm/scep v2.3.0 server and EJBCA Community Edition 9.6.3. Tested implementations lists what each run covers.

docs.title: Capabilities, answers and retries
docs.text: The client adapts each request to the capabilities the server lists, verifies every answer and retries when the server asks it to wait. This page explains those choices and the errors that come out of them.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
caps, err := client.GetCACaps(ctx)
if err != nil {
    return err
}
fmt.Println(caps.Has("Renewal"))

GetCACaps returns one entry per line of the answer with surrounding space and control characters removed, including a NUL byte that some servers append. Has compares names without regard to case. The client caches the list. The first PKIOperation fetches it when the program has not.

A server that answers GetCACaps with an HTTP error is treated as listing nothing. HTTP 503 is the exception: it means the server is busy, so the client returns the error instead.

docs.title: Algorithms
docs.text:
With a zero Digest and Encryption.ContentEncryption, the client picks from the capabilities:

Choice Rule HTTP method of PKIOperation POST when the server lists POSTPKIOperation or SCEPStandard, otherwise GET with the base64 message in the message parameter Signature digest SHA-256 when the server lists SHA-256 or SCEPStandard, else SHA-512, else SHA-1, else SHA-256 Content cipher DES-EDE3-CBC when the server lists DES3 but neither AES nor SCEPStandard, otherwise AES-128-CBC Key transport RSA PKCS #1 v1.5 unless Encryption.KeyEncryption selects RSAES-OAEP

A server that lists nothing gets GET, SHA-256 and AES-128-CBC.

docs.title: Verifying answers
docs.text:
For every PKIOperation answer the client:

  1. Reads the CertRep from a 200 OK answer. It also reads it from any other status when the content type is application/x-pki-message and the body is not empty. Some servers send PENDING with HTTP 202 or FAILURE with HTTP 400.
  2. Verifies the signature against CACertificates.Signers only. MD5 is accepted only when the request itself used MD5.
  3. Checks that the transactionID matches the request and that the recipientNonce repeats its senderNonce. A CertRep without a senderNonce of its own is accepted.
  4. Decrypts the content of a SUCCESS answer with the requester key. It accepts the ciphers in Options.Decrypt, AES-CBC and DES-EDE3-CBC by default, plus the cipher of the request.

A server that answers with single DES whatever the request used needs pkcs7.DESCBC in Options.Decrypt. Without it the client returns an error that wraps pkcs7.ErrContentEncryptionNotAllowed.

docs.title: HTTP errors
docs.text:
Any other answer becomes a *scepclient.HTTPError:

Field Content StatusCode The HTTP status RetryAfter The Retry-After header in seconds. Zero without the header Body Up to 256 bytes of the body on one line. It is empty when the body is not text, so binary data does not reach a terminal or a log ContentType The Content-Type header

Many servers explain a refusal in the body, so show Body to the user:

var httpErr *scepclient.HTTPError
if errors.As(err, &httpErr) {
    log.Printf("the server answered HTTP %d: %s", httpErr.StatusCode, httpErr.Body)
}

GetCACert, GetCACertChain and GetNextCACert return scepclient.ErrEmptyResponse for a 200 OK answer without a body, which some servers send for a missing CA name or an operation they lack.

docs.title: Busy servers
docs.text:
A server answers HTTP 503 to make a client wait. The client then sends the same message again:

Setting Default Effect Options.BusyRetries 3 How many times a request is sent again. A negative value turns retries off Retry-After header The wait in seconds, capped at five minutes. HTTP dates are ignored Options.BusyDelay 5 seconds The wait when the answer has no usable Retry-After header Options.OnBusy None Called before each wait with the answer and the delay 
client, err := scepclient.New(serverURL, scepclient.Options{
    BusyRetries: 5,
    OnBusy: func(answer *scepclient.HTTPError, delay time.Duration) {
        log.Printf("server busy (%s), retrying in %s", answer.Body, delay)
    },
})

When the retries run out, the 503 answer is returned as an *HTTPError. When the context ends during a wait, the error joins the 503 answer and the context error.

docs.title: Transport
docs.text:
The default HTTP client has a 60-second timeout. Set Options.HTTPClient for proxies, TLS settings or another timeout, for example to trust a private root for an https URL:

roots := x509.NewCertPool()
roots.AddCert(tlsRoot)
client, err := scepclient.New("https://ca.example.com/scep", scepclient.Options{
    HTTPClient: &http.Client{
        Timeout:   30 * time.Second,
        Transport: &http.Transport{TLSClientConfig: &tls.Config{RootCAs: roots}},
    },
})

Response bodies are limited to Options.MaxResponseBytes, 8 MiB by default, which leaves room for large CRLs. A larger answer is an error.

docs.title: CA certificates and trust
docs.text: Every request is encrypted for a CA or RA certificate. Every answer must be signed by one. A client gets these certificates with GetCACert. The answer is not signed, so the client checks it before it trusts it.

docs.title: Fetching the certificates
docs.text:
client, err := scepclient.New("https://ca.example.com/scep", scepclient.Options{})
if err != nil {
    return err
}
ca, err := client.GetCACert(ctx)
if err != nil {
    return err
}

New needs an http or https URL with a host. A server that serves several CAs on one URL picks the CA by name, which the client sends from Options.CAName. A server that needs a name may answer an empty 200 OK without one, which GetCACert returns as scepclient.ErrEmptyResponse.

The client reads a single DER or PEM certificate or a certificate-only SignedData, whatever content type the server sets.

docs.title: How the answer is sorted
docs.text:
GetCACert returns a *scepclient.CACertificates:

Field Content All Every certificate of the answer in server order CA The issuing CA certificate, which CertPoll, GetCert and GetCRL name as the issuer Recipients The certificates requests are encrypted for Signers The certificates allowed to sign CertRep messages

The certificates are sorted by these rules:

  • A certificate with the CA flag in its basic constraints is a CA certificate. Every other certificate is an RA certificate. A single certificate without basic constraints counts as the CA.
  • The issuing CA is the CA certificate that issued the RA certificates. Without RA certificates it is the CA certificate that issued none of the others, so in a root and intermediate chain it is the intermediate. Issuers are matched by name and key identifier, not by signature.
  • Recipients are the RA certificates with an RSA key whose key usage allows key or data encipherment or is absent. Without such an RA it is the CA certificate when its key is RSA.
  • Signers are the RA certificates whose key usage allows digital signatures or is absent, plus the issuing CA.

When no certificate has an RSA key, Recipients is empty and Enroll, Poll, GetCert and GetCRL return scepclient.ErrNoRSARecipient before they send anything.

When a server sends an RA certificate and the root but not the intermediate CA that issued the RA, no CA certificate issued the RA and the root becomes CA. Enrollment still works, because the RA certificate encrypts and signs, but a certificate issued under the intermediate does not verify against CA.

docs.title: Checking the certificates
docs.text:
The client never decides on its own whether a CA is genuine. Compare the CA certificate with a fingerprint the device received out of band, for example through provisioning or an MDM profile. Then check that the RA certificates were issued by that CA. The quickstart does both:

// checkCACertificates trusts a GetCACert answer only when the CA certificate has the fingerprint
// obtained out of band and every certificate that signs or decrypts for it was issued by that CA.
func checkCACertificates(ca *scepclient.CACertificates, fingerprint [32]byte) error {
    if sha256.Sum256(ca.CA.Raw) != fingerprint {
        return errors.New("the CA certificate does not match the pinned fingerprint")
    }
    for _, cert := range slices.Concat(ca.Signers, ca.Recipients) {
        if cert.Equal(ca.CA) {
            continue
        }
        if err := cert.CheckSignatureFrom(ca.CA); err != nil {
            return fmt.Errorf("RA certificate %s: %w", cert.Subject, err)
        }
    }
    return nil
}

CheckSignatureFrom refuses SHA-1 signatures, which some older CAs still put on their RA certificates. Pin the fingerprint of such an RA certificate as well or verify it with a library that accepts SHA-1.

A device that ships with its CA certificates can skip GetCACert. SortCACertificates sorts a list it loads itself into the same structure:

ca, err := scepclient.SortCACertificates([]*x509.Certificate{caCert, raCert})
if err != nil {
    return err
}

docs.title: Restricting the answer signers
docs.text: The client verifies every CertRep against Signers only. A certificate the CertRep carries itself is ignored, so an answer signed by any other key is refused even when it names an expected signer. An answer that carries no certificates verifies too.

docs.title: GetCACertChain
docs.text:
chain, err := client.GetCACertChain(ctx)

GetCACertChain returns the CA certificate and its issuers in server order. RFC 8894 does not define the operation and its answer carries no RA certificates, so enroll with the GetCACert answer. Check the chain before you trust it, for example by verifying chain[0] against a pinned root with x509.Certificate.Verify.

docs.title: CA rollover
docs.text:
A CA can announce the certificates that replace the current ones before they expire:

next, err := client.GetNextCACert(ctx, ca)
if err != nil {
    return err
}

The answer must be signed by one of ca.Signers, the certificates the device already trusts. GetNextCACert returns the new certificates sorted like a GetCACert answer. The client does not switch to them by itself. Store them and switch when the CA rolls over.

Servers without the operation answer in different ways. The handler of this module answers HTTP 501, which the client returns as *scepclient.HTTPError. A server that answers an empty 200 OK gives scepclient.ErrEmptyResponse.

docs.title: Certificates and CRLs
docs.text: GetCert fetches a certificate by its issuer and serial number. GetCRL fetches the CRL that covers a certificate. Both are PKIOperation requests, signed and encrypted like an enrollment. Both need a server that implements them.

docs.title: Fetching a certificate
docs.text:
certs, err := client.GetCert(ctx, ca, scepclient.QueryRequest{
    SerialNumber:      cert.SerialNumber,
    SignerCertificate: cert,
    SignerKey:         key,
})
if err != nil {
    return err
}
fetched := certs[0]

QueryRequest names the certificate and the requester:

Field Meaning Issuer The DER encoded name of the issuing CA. The zero value takes the subject of ca.CA SerialNumber The serial number of the certificate SignerCertificate, SignerKey Sign the request. The key decrypts the answer, so it must be an RSA crypto.Decrypter. Servers usually expect a certificate the CA issued Digest, Encryption As in EnrollRequest

GetCert returns the certificates of the answer in server order. The handler of this module sends the requested certificate first.

docs.title: Fetching a CRL
docs.text:
der, err := client.GetCRL(ctx, ca, scepclient.QueryRequest{
    SerialNumber:      cert.SerialNumber,
    SignerCertificate: cert,
    SignerKey:         key,
})
if err != nil {
    return err
}
crl, err := x509.ParseRevocationList(der)
if err != nil {
    return err
}
if err := crl.CheckSignatureFrom(ca.CA); err != nil {
    return err
}

GetCRL returns the DER encoded CRL. The CertRep that carries it is signed by a trusted CA or RA certificate, but the client does not check the CRL itself. Check its signature and its NextUpdate before you rely on it.

docs.title: Refusals
docs.text:
A FAILURE answer returns a *scepclient.FailureError with the failInfo. A PENDING answer, which these requests do not expect, returns the same error type with Status set to PENDING:

var failure *scepclient.FailureError
if errors.As(err, &failure) && failure.FailInfo == scep.BadCertID {
    return fmt.Errorf("the CA does not know serial %s: %w", cert.SerialNumber, err)
}

A server without the operation may answer FAILURE with badRequest, as the handler of this module does. Other servers answer with an HTTP error, which the client returns as *scepclient.HTTPError.

docs.title: Enrollment and renewal
docs.text: A device enrolls with a PKCSReq, waits while the CA keeps the request pending and later renews with a RenewalReq. Each request needs the sorted CA certificates from CA certificates and trust.

docs.title: Creating the CSR
docs.text:
A PKCSReq usually carries a challenge password in the CSR, which crypto/x509 cannot add. x509util.CreateCertificateRequest creates the CSR with it:

der, err := x509util.CreateCertificateRequest(rand.Reader, &x509util.CertificateRequest{
    Subject:           pkix.Name{CommonName: "device-42"},
    DNSNames:          []string{"device-42.example.com"},
    ChallengePassword: password,
}, key)
if err != nil {
    return err
}
csr, err := x509.ParseCertificateRequest(der)
if err != nil {
    return err
}

CertificateRequest embeds x509.CertificateRequest, so the usual template fields apply. With a challenge password the key must be RSA or ECDSA on P-224, P-256, P-384 or P-521. The template SignatureAlgorithm is honored, including the RSA-PSS algorithms. Without a password the function returns the CSR crypto/x509 creates.

docs.title: Enrolling with a PKCSReq
docs.text:
The quickstart enrolls a new RSA key:

// enroll creates an RSA key and a CSR with the challenge password and enrolls it with a PKCSReq.
func enroll(ctx context.Context, client *scepclient.Client, ca *scepclient.CACertificates, password string) (*x509.Certificate, *rsa.PrivateKey, error) {
    key, err := rsa.GenerateKey(rand.Reader, 2048)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, nil, err
    }
    der, err := x509util.CreateCertificateRequest(rand.Reader, &x509util.CertificateRequest{
        Subject:           pkix.Name{CommonName: "quickstart-device"},
        ChallengePassword: password,
    }, key)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, nil, err
    }
    csr, err := x509.ParseCertificateRequest(der)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, nil, err
    }
    // A PKCSReq is signed with a self-signed certificate for the CSR key. The answer is encrypted
    // for that certificate.
    signer, err := selfSigned(key, csr.Subject)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, nil, err
    }
    res, err := client.EnrollAndWait(ctx, ca, scepclient.EnrollRequest{
        CSR:               csr,
        SignerCertificate: signer,
        SignerKey:         key,
    }, 5*time.Second)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, nil, err
    }
    if res.Status != scep.SUCCESS {
        return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("enrollment answered %s %s", res.Status, res.FailInfo)
    }
    return res.Certificate, key, nil
}

// selfSigned returns a short-lived self-signed certificate for key.
func selfSigned(key *rsa.PrivateKey, subject pkix.Name) (*x509.Certificate, error) {
    template := &x509.Certificate{
        SerialNumber: randomSerial(),
        Subject:      subject,
        NotBefore:    time.Now().Add(-time.Hour),
        NotAfter:     time.Now().Add(time.Hour),
        KeyUsage:     x509.KeyUsageDigitalSignature | x509.KeyUsageKeyEncipherment,
    }
    der, err := x509.CreateCertificate(rand.Reader, template, template, &key.PublicKey, key)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    return x509.ParseCertificate(der)
}

EnrollRequest describes the request:

Field Meaning MessageType scep.PKCSReq (the default) or scep.RenewalReq CSR The certificate request. Its public key identifies the issued certificate in the answer SignerCertificate, SignerKey Sign the request. The key also decrypts the answer, so it must be an RSA crypto.Decrypter. A PKCSReq uses a self-signed certificate for the CSR key TransactionID Identifies the enrollment. The zero value derives it from the CSR key with scep.CSRTransactionID Digest, Encryption The signature digest and the content cipher and key transport. Zero values follow the server capabilities, see Capabilities, answers and retries

Enroll and EnrollAndWait return a *scepclient.Result:

Field Content Status scep.SUCCESS, scep.PENDING or scep.FAILURE FailInfo The reason of a FAILURE Certificate The issued certificate, the one whose public key is the CSR key Certificates Every certificate of a SUCCESS answer in server order, such as the chain TransactionID The transaction ID, which Poll needs Response The verified CertRep

A FAILURE answer is a result, not an error. The error is set when the request could not be sent, the server answered without a CertRep or the answer did not verify. A SUCCESS answer without a certificate for the CSR key is an error too.

docs.title: Devices with ECDSA keys
docs.text:
The answer is encrypted for the certificate that signs the request, with RSA key transport. A device whose CSR key is ECDSA signs the PKCSReq with a separate RSA key and a self-signed certificate for it. The CA issues the certificate for the ECDSA key in the CSR:

res, err := client.Enroll(ctx, ca, scepclient.EnrollRequest{
    CSR:               ecdsaCSR,
    SignerCertificate: rsaSignerCert,
    SignerKey:         rsaSignerKey,
})

res.Certificate then holds the ECDSA key. With a SignerKey that is not RSA, Enroll sends nothing and returns scepclient: the signer key must be an RSA crypto.Decrypter. The handler of this module answers FAILURE with badAlg when another client signs a request with such a key.

docs.title: Waiting for approval
docs.text:
EnrollAndWait sends the request and, while the CA answers PENDING, polls with CertPoll every interval:

ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 30*time.Minute)
defer cancel()
res, err := client.EnrollAndWait(ctx, ca, req, time.Minute)

It returns the first SUCCESS or FAILURE result. When the context ends first, it returns the last PENDING result together with the context error, so set a deadline that matches how long an approval may take. The interval must be positive.

A device that stops and polls later keeps the CSR, the signer certificate and key and the transaction ID, then sends one CertPoll at a time with Poll:

res, err := client.Poll(ctx, ca, scepclient.EnrollRequest{
    CSR:               csr,
    SignerCertificate: signerCert,
    SignerKey:         signerKey,
    TransactionID:     savedTransactionID,
})

Poll derives the transaction ID from the CSR when TransactionID is empty, which matches an enrollment that used the default.

docs.title: Renewing with a RenewalReq
docs.text:
A RenewalReq is signed with the certificate being renewed and its key, which the CA uses to authorize the request. The quickstart renews for a new key:

// renew requests a certificate for a new key with a RenewalReq signed by the current certificate.
func renew(ctx context.Context, client *scepclient.Client, ca *scepclient.CACertificates, cert *x509.Certificate, key *rsa.PrivateKey) (*x509.Certificate, error) {
    newKey, err := rsa.GenerateKey(rand.Reader, 2048)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    der, err := x509.CreateCertificateRequest(rand.Reader, &x509.CertificateRequest{Subject: cert.Subject}, newKey)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    csr, err := x509.ParseCertificateRequest(der)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    res, err := client.Enroll(ctx, ca, scepclient.EnrollRequest{
        MessageType:       scep.RenewalReq,
        CSR:               csr,
        SignerCertificate: cert,
        SignerKey:         key,
    })
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    if res.Status != scep.SUCCESS {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("renewal answered %s %s", res.Status, res.FailInfo)
    }
    return res.Certificate, nil
}

The current key decrypts the answer, so it must be RSA. The CSR may carry a new key or the current one. The client sends a RenewalReq whether or not the server lists the Renewal capability. Check GetCACaps first when you need to fall back to a PKCSReq with a new challenge password.

Enroll sends PKCSReq and RenewalReq only. Build an UpdateReq from earlier SCEP drafts with scep.NewCSRRequest from the message layer.

docs.title: Choosing the algorithms
docs.text:
The client picks the digest and the cipher from the server capabilities. Set them on the request to override that choice, for example AES-256-CBC with RSAES-OAEP key transport for a server that accepts both:

req.Encryption = pkcs7.EncryptOptions{
    ContentEncryption: pkcs7.AES256CBC,
    KeyEncryption:     pkcs7.RSAOAEP,
}

The answer comes back with RSA PKCS #1 v1.5 key transport from the handler of this module, which always uses it for answers.

docs.title: Development
docs.text: How to build, check and change the library. Contribution rules are in CONTRIBUTING.md.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Go at the version go.mod declares.
  • Python 3 with the MkDocs toolchain for the documentation site, installed by make docs-deps from packages pinned by hash.
  • sscep and the micromdm/scep client for the interop tests, see Testing.

golangci-lint, actionlint, govulncheck, gitleaks and cyclonedx-gomod are downloaded into bin/ at pinned versions by the Make targets that need them.

docs.text: Path Content root package scep The pkiMessage layer: building, parsing, decrypting and answering scepserver/ The HTTP handler and the CA interfaces scepclient/ The HTTP client and the sorting of CA certificates x509util/ CSRs with a challenge password, partly copied from the Go standard library cryptoutil/ Key identifiers for transaction IDs internal/testca/ The in-memory CA the tests run against examples/ Runnable programs, built and tested with the root module testdata/ Message fixtures with their test certificates and keys docs/ This site

docs.title: Common commands
docs.text:
make fmt-check    # fail when a tracked Go file is not gofmt formatted
make lint         # golangci-lint at the version CI uses
make test         # go vet and the tests under the race detector
make fuzz         # each fuzz target for FUZZTIME, 30s by default
make interop      # sscep and micromdm/scep against the module
make docs-build   # strict MkDocs build
make help         # every target

Run make tidy-check when go.mod changes, make govulncheck when a dependency changes and make actionlint when a workflow changes. make gitleaks scans the working tree and the commit history for credentials.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The site is built with MkDocs and the Material theme from docs/ and mkdocs.yml. Set PYTHON when the MkDocs toolchain lives in a virtual environment:

make docs-deps PYTHON=.venv/bin/python
make docs-serve PYTHON=.venv/bin/python

make docs-build runs with --strict, so a broken link, a missing anchor or a page absent from the navigation fails the build. Pages include code from examples/quickstart and from Example in example_test.go through snippet markers, so that code is compiled and run by make test. Keep the --8<-- marker lines when you edit those files. CI runs the same build on every change to the documentation and publishes the site from main.

docs.title: Continuous integration
docs.text: Workflow Runs Tests Tidy and format checks, the build, the tests and 30 seconds of each fuzz target on Linux, the tests on macOS and the build on Windows Lint golangci-lint, its configuration check and actionlint Interop sscep, micromdm/scep and EJBCA against the module, also weekly Supply chain govulncheck and gitleaks, also weekly CodeQL and Scorecard Static analysis and the OpenSSF Scorecard checks Documentation The strict site build and publishing from main Release The release artifacts for a version tag, see Release process

docs.title: Release process
docs.text: A release starts when a version tag reachable from main is pushed. CHANGELOG.md has one section per version. That section becomes the release description.

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text: The module follows semantic versioning under the Compatibility policy. Release tags are stable versions such as v0.1.0. The release workflow refuses any other tag form.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. On dev, complete the section of the new version in CHANGELOG.md and date it on the release day.

  2. Run the checks:

    make lint
make test
make docs-build
VERSION=vX.Y.Z make release-check

    The release check exports HEAD with git archive, then verifies, builds, vets and tests the export and imports it from a separate module. It catches files that are untracked or only present locally. With VERSION set it also checks that the changelog has a dated heading for the version and no Unreleased section.

  3. Merge dev into main, create a signed tag and push main and the tag:

    git tag -s vX.Y.Z -m 'vX.Y.Z'
git push origin main vX.Y.Z

  4. The release workflow checks that the tag belongs to the default branch, repeats the release check, builds source archives, an SBOM and checksums, attests their provenance and creates a draft release with the changelog section as its description. Review the draft and publish it.

Do not publish a release from the GitHub UI. Publishing creates the tag, which starts the workflow. The workflow then refuses to rebuild a release that is already published. To recover, delete the release and its tag with gh release delete vX.Y.Z --cleanup-tag --yes and push the tag again. A draft that already exists for the tag is updated with the new assets and description. The workflow can also be started by hand for an existing tag.

docs.title: Release assets
docs.text: Asset Content go-pki-scep-vX.Y.Z-source.zip and .tar.gz The complete tagged source tree go-pki-scep-vX.Y.Z-sbom.cdx.json A CycloneDX software bill of materials go-pki-scep-vX.Y.Z_SHA256SUMS.txt SHA-256 checksums of the archives and the SBOM go-pki-scep-vX.Y.Z.intoto.jsonl The signed build provenance of the assets

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: The library is tested at three levels. Each package has unit tests. Fuzz targets cover the parser and the handler. The Interop workflow runs other SCEP implementations against the module.

docs.title: Unit tests
docs.text:
make test

Runs go vet and every test under the race detector.

  • The scep tests build, parse, decrypt and answer every message type, check the algorithm choices of answers, the restriction to expected signers and the nonce and transaction ID checks, and parse captured messages from testdata.
  • The scepserver tests drive the handler with internal/testca: every operation and method, the size limits, the refusals and their failInfo values, the CA outcomes, the refusal recorder and the log levels.
  • The scepclient tests run the client against the handler and against test servers that reproduce server behavior outside RFC 8894, such as answers with a NUL byte, an empty body, HTTP 503, HTTP 202 and single DES.
  • Example in example_test.go and the tests of examples/quickstart run the code the documentation shows.

docs.title: Fuzzing
docs.text:
make fuzz
make fuzz FUZZTIME=2m

Runs two fuzz targets for FUZZTIME each, 30 seconds by default:

Target Checks FuzzParsePKIMessage Parsing, decrypting and answering hostile messages returns errors instead of panicking FuzzPKIOperation The handler answers any POST body with a client error or a CertRep, never with a panic or HTTP 500

CI runs 30 seconds of each target on every push and pull request. Go writes a failing input under the package's testdata/fuzz directory. Commit that input with the fix so it stays a regression test.

docs.title: Interop tests
docs.text:
make interop

The interop tests have the interop build tag and run real SCEP peers against the module. make interop runs the sscep and micromdm/scep tests and skips each one whose peer is missing. SCEP_INTEROP=required turns a skip into a failure, as in CI. INTEROP_RUN selects the tests:

make interop INTEROP_RUN=TestSSCEP
Test Peer Environment TestSSCEP sscep against the handler SSCEP, else sscep on the PATH TestMicroMDMClient The micromdm/scep client against the handler MICROMDM_SCEPCLIENT, else scepclient on the PATH TestMicroMDMServer The client against a running micromdm/scep server SCEP_INTEROP_MICROMDM_URL, SCEP_INTEROP_MICROMDM_CHALLENGE TestEJBCAServer The client against a running EJBCA SCEP_INTEROP_EJBCA_URL, SCEP_INTEROP_EJBCA_CA, SCEP_INTEROP_EJBCA_CHALLENGE

The Interop workflow builds each peer, starts the servers and sets these variables. Tested implementations describes what each test covers.

docs.title: Tested implementations
docs.text: The Interop workflow runs other SCEP implementations against the handler and the client on every push and pull request to dev and main and once a week. The peers are built from pinned sources or run from images pinned by digest. A peer that is missing fails the run instead of being skipped.

docs.title: Clients against the handler
docs.text:
The handler serves internal/testca, an in-memory RSA CA with a challenge password.

Client Version What the run covers sscep v0.10.0, commit b3f9798 getcaps. getca returns the CA certificate. enroll with AES and SHA-256: the CA answers PENDING and issues on the first CertPoll. getcert fetches the issued certificate by serial number. getcrl fetches a CRL signed by the CA micromdm/scep scepclient v2.3.0 Enrollment with a challenge password. The issued certificate has the requested subject and verifies against the CA

The micromdm/scep v2.3.0 client encrypts with single DES, the default of the smallstep/pkcs7 v0.1.1 library it uses. The test therefore adds pkcs7.DESCBC to the handler Options.Decrypt. It does not assert which cipher the client chose.

docs.title: The client against servers
docs.text:
Server Version What the run covers micromdm/scep scepserver v2.3.0 GetCACaps and GetCACert. A PKCSReq with the challenge password gets SUCCESS and a certificate that verifies against the CA. A wrong challenge password gets FAILURE EJBCA Community Edition 9.6.3, image keyfactor/ejbca-ce:9.6.3 GetCACaps and GetCACert with a CA name. GetCACertChain returns the issuing CA and its root. A PKCSReq with the end entity password gets SUCCESS. A second request with the same password gets FAILURE. A wrong password gets HTTP 401 and a missing one HTTP 400, both without a CertRep

The micromdm/scep v2.3.0 server encrypts its answers with the same single DES default. The test therefore adds pkcs7.DESCBC to the client Options.Decrypt for that run. It does not assert which cipher the server chose.

EJBCA runs with two RSA CAs, a root and an issuing CA. Its SCEP alias runs in CA mode, where the CSR common name names the end entity and its password is the challenge password. The client sets Options.CAName to the issuing CA.

docs.title: Running the tests locally
docs.text:
The interop tests have the interop build tag. make interop runs the sscep and micromdm/scep tests and skips each one whose peer is missing:

make interop

Point SSCEP and MICROMDM_SCEPCLIENT at the client binaries when they are not on the PATH. The tests against servers need a running server: set SCEP_INTEROP_MICROMDM_URL and SCEP_INTEROP_MICROMDM_CHALLENGE for micromdm/scep. Set SCEP_INTEROP_EJBCA_URL, SCEP_INTEROP_EJBCA_CA and SCEP_INTEROP_EJBCA_CHALLENGE for EJBCA and run make interop INTEROP_RUN=TestEJBCAServer. The workflow file shows how CI starts each peer.

docs.title: Other servers
docs.text:
The client copes with server behavior that RFC 8894 does not require. Unit tests in scepclient simulate each case. The CertRep without a senderNonce or certificates is tested in the scep package, whose parser the client uses:

  • A capability list that ends with a NUL byte.
  • An empty 200 OK to GetCACert, GetCACertChain or GetNextCACert, returned as scepclient.ErrEmptyResponse.
  • A CertRep without a senderNonce or without certificates.
  • A CertRep signed with SHA-1.
  • A PENDING CertRep with HTTP 202 and a FAILURE CertRep with HTTP 400.
  • HTTP 503 with or without a Retry-After header.
  • A GetCACert answer as a PEM certificate.
  • An answer encrypted with single DES whatever the request used, when Options.Decrypt allows it.

certrally, a command line client built on this library, records the behavior of further SCEP servers in its interoperability notes.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Start with the handler log on the server side and the error text on the client side. The handler logs the cause of every refusal, which it does not send to the client, as Refusals and logging describes.

docs.title: Server side
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix FAILURE with badAlg, cause the request signer certificate has no RSA key The device signs with an ECDSA or other non-RSA key The device must sign with an RSA key, see Devices with ECDSA keys FAILURE with badAlg, cause content encryption algorithm is not allowed The device encrypts with a cipher Options.Decrypt does not accept, usually single DES Add pkcs7.DESCBC to Options.Decrypt for those devices FAILURE with badMessageCheck The pkiEnvelope does not decrypt with the responder key Check that Responder returns the key of the certificate the device encrypted for HTTP 400, reason malformed or unverifiable pkiMessage The message does not parse, its signature does not verify, it is signed with MD5 or its certificate marks the authority key identifier critical. The cause signing time ... is outside of certificate validity means the signer certificate was expired or not yet valid at the signing-time, for example a RenewalReq signed with an expired certificate Read the cause in the log. Set Options.AllowMD5 for MD5 devices and Options.LegacyCertificateParser for the Windows clients that send such certificates. A device whose certificate expired enrolls again with a PKCSReq HTTP 400, reason the pkiEnvelope is not addressed to this CA Responder returned ErrNotFound for every recipient, often because the device still holds an old CA or RA certificate Compare the recipient issuer and serial number with your certificates. Serve the old identity until devices have fetched the new one HTTP 413 or 414 The message is larger than Options.MaxMessageBytes Raise the limit, for example for large RSA keys or long certificate chains HTTP 500, log scep request failed The CA returned no certificates or an error that is not ErrPending, *Failure or *Busy Read the error attribute of the log record HTTP 501 GetCACertChain or GetNextCACert to a CA without the interface Implement ChainGetter or NextCAGetter. Ignore it when the operation is not needed

docs.title: Client side
docs.text: Error Cause Fix scepclient.ErrEmptyResponse from GetCACert The server needs a CA name Set Options.CAName scepclient.ErrNoRSARecipient No certificate in the GetCACert answer has an RSA key The CA needs an RSA RA certificate scepclient: the signer key must be an RSA crypto.Decrypter SignerKey is not RSA Sign with a separate RSA key and a self-signed certificate scep: verify pkiMessage The answer is not signed by a certificate in CACertificates.Signers Fetch the CA certificates again. When you pin them, build the list with SortCACertificates and include the RA signing certificate An error that wraps pkcs7.ErrContentEncryptionNotAllowed The server answers with single DES Add pkcs7.DESCBC to Options.Decrypt *scepclient.HTTPError with status 503 The server stayed busy longer than the retries Raise BusyRetries or BusyDelay or try later *scepclient.HTTPError with another status The server refused without a CertRep. EJBCA, for example, answers a wrong challenge password with HTTP 401 and a missing one with HTTP 400 Read Body and the server log the SUCCESS answer holds no certificate for the CSR key The server issued a certificate for another key Check the CSR the device sent and the CA configuration Result.Status FAILURE The CA refused the request, for example for a wrong challenge password Check the password and the subject with the CA operator EnrollAndWait returns context.DeadlineExceeded with a PENDING result Nobody approved the request in time Extend the deadline or store the request and call Poll later

docs.title: Gathering information
docs.text:
Before reporting a problem, collect:

  • the go-pki-scep and Go versions
  • the other side and its version
  • the GetCACaps answer
  • the handler log record or the client error text
  • where possible, the request and the answer from a test with throwaway keys

Never share private keys, challenge passwords or messages captured from a production system.

docs.title: Client options
docs.text: scepclient.New(serverURL, opts) returns a client for one SCEP URL. The zero Options value is usable. New returns an error for a URL without an http or https scheme or without a host and for a negative MaxResponseBytes.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Field Type Default Effect HTTPClient *http.Client A client with a DefaultTimeout timeout of 60 seconds Sends the requests. Set it for proxies, TLS settings or another timeout CAName string Empty Sent as the message parameter of GetCACaps, GetCACert, GetCACertChain and GetNextCACert. Servers with several CAs on one URL pick the CA by it MaxResponseBytes int64 DefaultMaxResponseBytes, 8 MiB The largest response body BusyRetries int DefaultBusyRetries, 3 How often a request is sent again after HTTP 503. A negative value turns retries off BusyDelay time.Duration DefaultBusyDelay, 5 seconds The wait after HTTP 503 without a Retry-After header in seconds Decrypt pkcs7.DecryptOptions AES-128-CBC, AES-192-CBC, AES-256-CBC and DES-EDE3-CBC The ciphers accepted in SUCCESS answers. The cipher of the request is always accepted. Add pkcs7.DESCBC for servers that answer with single DES OnBusy func(*HTTPError, time.Duration) None Called before each wait that follows HTTP 503

A Retry-After delay is capped at five minutes.

SortCACertificates(certs) sorts certificates the caller loaded itself into a *CACertificates.

It must be an RSA crypto.Decrypter TransactionID scep.CSRTransactionID(CSR) The transaction ID Digest Picked from the capabilities The signature digest Encryption Cipher picked from the capabilities, PKCS #1 v1.5 key transport The content cipher and key transport
