docs.text: Name Value DefaultTimeout 60 seconds DefaultMaxResponseBytes 8 MiB DefaultBusyRetries 3 DefaultBusyDelay 5 seconds

docs.title: Compatibility policy
docs.text: The module uses semantic versioning. Its public API is every exported identifier of the scep, scepserver, scepclient, x509util and cryptoutil packages. internal/testca and the programs under examples are not part of it.

docs.title: Before v1.0.0
docs.text: A minor release may change the public API. CHANGELOG.md describes every change that affects callers, including any that needs a code change.

docs.title: Optional interfaces
docs.text: The handler finds the optional CA interfaces, CertificateGetter, CRLGetter, NextCAGetter, ChainGetter and RefusalRecorder, with type assertions at run time. A CA that lacks one still compiles and the handler falls back as Optional operations describes. A method added to scepserver.CA itself is a compile error that names what to implement.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
1. Read the CHANGELOG section of each version between yours and the new one.
  2. Run go get github.com/misiektoja/go-pki-scep@vX.Y.Z and build.
  3. Run your tests against the SCEP clients or servers you support. Tested implementations names the versions the Interop workflow runs.

docs.title: Go version
docs.text: The module declares the minimum Go version in go.mod, currently 1.27.3. CI builds and tests with exactly that version.

docs.title: Status values
docs.text:
A CertRep carries a pkiStatus and, on FAILURE, a failInfo. The scep package defines both as string types holding the decimal value. Their String methods print the name and the number, as in FAILURE (2).

pkiStatus Value Meaning scep.SUCCESS 0 The answer carries the certificates or the CRL scep.FAILURE 2 The request was refused. The failInfo gives the reason scep.PENDING 3 The CA has not decided. The requester polls with CertPoll failInfo Value Sent by this module's handler for scep.BadAlg 0 A request signed with a key that is not RSA. A request encrypted with a cipher or key transport the handler does not accept scep.BadMessageCheck 1 A pkiEnvelope that does not decrypt with the responder key scep.BadRequest 2 A pkiEnvelope with an invalid CSR or query. GetCert or GetCRL to a CA without them scep.BadTime 3 Only when the CA returns it scep.BadCertID 4 Only when the CA returns it

The CA can return any of the five values in a *scepserver.Failure. Fail refuses any other value.

docs.title: Message types
docs.text:
Constant Value scep.CertRep 3 scep.RenewalReq 17 scep.UpdateReq 18 scep.PKCSReq 19 scep.CertPoll 20 scep.GetCert 21 scep.GetCRL 22

ParsePKIMessage refuses any other message type.

docs.title: Server errors
docs.text: Error Returned by Answer scepserver.ErrPending Enroll, Poll CertRep PENDING *scepserver.Failure Any CA method that answers with a CertRep CertRep FAILURE with Info. Err is logged only *scepserver.Busy Any CA method that answers with a CertRep HTTP 503 with Retry-After scepserver.ErrNotFound from CACertificates, CACertificateChain or NextCACertificates The CA HTTP 404 scepserver.ErrNotFound from Responder for every recipient The CA HTTP 400 scepserver.ErrSignerNotRSA The handler, as Failure.Err CertRep FAILURE with badAlg Any other error The CA HTTP 500 with the body internal error

docs.title: Client errors
docs.text:
Error Cause *scepclient.HTTPError An answer that is not 200 OK and carries no CertRep *scepclient.FailureError A FAILURE or PENDING answer to GetCert or GetCRL scepclient.ErrEmptyResponse A 200 OK without a body to GetCACert, GetCACertChain or GetNextCACert scepclient.ErrNoRSARecipient CA certificates without an RSA certificate to encrypt for. Returned before a request is sent Wraps pkcs7.ErrContentEncryptionNotAllowed A SUCCESS answer encrypted with a cipher that Options.Decrypt does not accept Wraps pkcs7.ErrDecryptionFailed A SUCCESS answer that does not decrypt with the requester key scep: verify pkiMessage An answer not signed by one of CACertificates.Signers scep: CertRep transactionID ... does not match or recipientNonce does not match An answer to another request

Enroll, Poll and EnrollAndWait report FAILURE and PENDING in Result.Status, not as an error.

docs.title: Errors of the message layer
docs.text: ParsePKIMessage, DecryptPKIEnvelope and the request and answer builders return errors that start with scep: and wrap the go-pkcs7 error where there is one. Use errors.Is with the go-pkcs7 sentinel errors, such as pkcs7.ErrDecryptionFailed or pkcs7.ErrContentEncryptionNotAllowed, to tell causes apart.

docs.title: Server options
docs.text: scepserver.NewHandler(ca, opts) returns the handler. The zero Options value is usable.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Field Type Default Effect Capabilities []string Derived, see Capabilities Replaces the GetCACaps answer. Each entry must be one non-empty line Decrypt pkcs7.DecryptOptions AES-128-CBC, AES-192-CBC, AES-256-CBC and DES-EDE3-CBC The content ciphers accepted in requests. Add pkcs7.DESCBC only for clients that cannot send anything stronger AllowMD5 bool false Accepts requests signed with the MD5 digest LegacyCertificateParser bool false Accepts requester certificates that mark the authority key identifier critical, which some Windows SCEP clients send Digest crypto.Hash Follow the request, see below The signature digest of CertRep messages and GetNextCACert answers ContentEncryption pkcs7.ContentEncryptionAlgorithm Follow the request The cipher of CertRep content. Set it for clients that send one cipher but decrypt another MaxMessageBytes int64 DefaultMaxMessageBytes, 64 KiB The largest PKIOperation message, measured before base64 encoding for GET Logger *slog.Logger Discards records Receives the records listed in Refusals and logging

With a zero Digest, a CertRep uses the request digest when it is MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512 and SHA-256 otherwise. A GetNextCACert answer uses SHA-256.

NewHandler returns an error for a nil CA, a negative MaxMessageBytes or a capability that is empty or contains a line break.

A PKCSReq with a 4096-bit RSA key and its self-signed certificate takes about 6 KiB, so the default limit leaves room. A GET request carries the message base64 encoded, so its message parameter may be about a third longer than the limit, plus a margin for line breaks.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
Without Options.Capabilities the handler lists, in this order:

Capability Listed when AES Decrypt accepts an AES cipher, as it does by default DES3 Decrypt accepts DES-EDE3-CBC, as it does by default GetNextCACert The CA implements NextCAGetter POSTPKIOperation Always Renewal Always SCEPStandard Decrypt accepts an AES cipher SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-512 Always

The answer is one capability per line, each followed by a line feed, with the content type text/plain; charset=utf-8. A replaced list is sent as given. The handler does not check that it matches what the handler supports.

docs.title: HTTP interface
docs.text:
Operation Methods Parameters GetCACaps GET message is ignored GetCACert GET message is the CA name passed to CACertificates GetCACertChain GET message is the CA name passed to CACertificateChain GetNextCACert GET message is the CA name passed to NextCACertificates PKIOperation GET and POST GET carries the base64 pkiMessage in message. POST carries the DER pkiMessage as the body

In a GET message, a space is read as + and line breaks are removed, because some clients leave the base64 text unescaped or split it into lines. Optional operations lists the answer formats and Refusals and logging the error answers.

docs.title: Constants and errors
docs.text:
Name Meaning DefaultMaxMessageBytes 64 KiB, the default MaxMessageBytes ErrPending Returned by Enroll or Poll to answer PENDING ErrNotFound Returned for an unknown CA name, recipient or next CA certificate ErrSignerNotRSA The cause of the badAlg answer to a request signed with a key that is not RSA *Failure Refuses a request with a failInfo *Busy Asks the client to retry, answered with HTTP 503

Errors and status values describes how each one reaches the client.

docs.title: Security model
docs.text: This page states what the library checks, what it leaves to the code that embeds it and which defaults protect both sides. Report vulnerabilities as the security policy describes.

docs.title: What a SCEP message protects
docs.text:
A pkiMessage is signed and its content is encrypted. Requests are encrypted for the CA or RA certificate, so the CSR and the challenge password are readable only by the holder of that key. Answers are encrypted for the certificate that signed the request. The signature covers the encrypted content, so a changed envelope breaks the signature.

The HTTP transport adds nothing to this. Over plain HTTP the GetCACaps and GetCACert answers and the fact that a device enrolls are visible and can be changed on the path. HTTPS hides them, but a device still needs a trusted CA fingerprint for the GetCACert answer.

docs.title: What the handler checks
docs.text:
• The signature of each request, with the certificate the request carries. This proves that the requester holds the signer key. Any key can sign a request with a self-signed certificate.
  • That the signing-time of a request, when present, falls within the validity of the signer certificate. The attribute is optional and the signer chooses its value, so it does not prove that the certificate is valid now.
  • That the pkiEnvelope is addressed to an identity the CA returns from Responder.
  • That the request signer key is RSA, so the answer can be encrypted for it.
  • That the pkiEnvelope decrypts with an accepted cipher.
  • For an enrollment, that the CSR signature is valid.
  • The size of each PKIOperation message. A POST body is not read past MaxMessageBytes.

docs.title: What the CA decides
docs.text:
The handler does not authorize anyone. The CA decides:

  • whether the challenge password of a PKCSReq is valid, compared in constant time
  • whether the certificate that signs a RenewalReq was issued by the CA, is valid now and is not revoked, because the signing-time check of the handler does not settle that
  • which subjects, names and key types a requester may get
  • whether a CertPoll comes from the requester of the enrollment, because the answer is encrypted for the CertPoll signer
  • who may fetch which certificate with GetCert and which CRL with GetCRL
  • how often a device may poll, through *scepserver.Busy

Rate limits per client belong in HTTP middleware in front of the handler.

docs.title: What the client checks
docs.text:
• Nothing about the GetCACert answer. The caller checks the CA certificate against a fingerprint it trusts before it uses the answer.
  • That each CertRep is signed by one of CACertificates.Signers. Certificates carried in the answer cannot replace them.
  • That the transactionID and the recipientNonce of each CertRep match the request, so an answer to another request is refused.
  • That GetNextCACert answers are signed by the current CA or RA.
  • The size of each response body and the Retry-After delay a server can ask for.

docs.title: Algorithm defaults
docs.text:
Area Default Opt-in for older peers Signature digest SHA-256 SHA-1 when a server lists SHA-1 but not SHA-256, SHA-512 or SCEPStandard. MD5 through Digest on the sending side and AllowMD5 on the handler Content cipher AES-128-CBC. AES-CBC and DES-EDE3-CBC are accepted Single DES through Decrypt on either side Key transport RSA PKCS #1 v1.5 RSAES-OAEP for requests through Encryption.KeyEncryption

PKCS #1 v1.5 key transport is what SCEP peers use. go-pkcs7 decrypts it with the countermeasure of RFC 3218, so a failed decryption returns pkcs7.ErrDecryptionFailed whatever step failed. The handler answers all of them with badMessageCheck, so a sender learns nothing about the padding.

docs.title: Information sent to clients
docs.text: HTTP refusals carry a fixed reason. Failure.Err and internal errors are logged and never sent. The client keeps at most 256 bytes of an error body in HTTPError.Body on one line. It drops a body that is not text, so a hostile server cannot put control characters into a terminal or a log through it.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text: The handler logs transaction IDs, message types, statuses, failInfo values and the causes the CA and the handler give. It never logs challenge passwords or CSRs. Keep secrets out of Failure.Err, because it is logged.

docs.title: Not provided
docs.text:
• No storage. Pending requests, issued certificates and revocation state live in the CA.
  • No TLS termination and no rate limiting.
  • No password-based encryption of answers (PasswordRecipientInfo), so requesters need RSA keys to receive an answer.

docs.title: Implementing a CA
docs.text:
The handler does the protocol work and calls your CA for every decision. A CA implements scepserver.CA, shown here without its comments:

type CA interface {
    CACertificates(ctx context.Context, name string) ([]*x509.Certificate, error)
    Responder(ctx context.Context, recipient scep.IssuerAndSerial) (*Responder, error)
    Enroll(ctx context.Context, req *Request) ([]*x509.Certificate, error)
    Poll(ctx context.Context, req *Request) ([]*x509.Certificate, error)
}
Method Called for Returns CACertificates GetCACert The CA certificate first, then the RA certificates when an RA answers for the CA Responder Every PKIOperation The identity whose decrypter certificate has the issuer and serial number the pkiEnvelope names Enroll PKCSReq, RenewalReq and UpdateReq The issued certificate first, optionally followed by its chain Poll CertPoll The certificate of an earlier enrollment once it is issued

Optional interfaces add GetCert, GetCRL, GetNextCACert and GetCACertChain, as Optional operations describes. The handler calls the CA methods concurrently, so the CA guards its own state.

docs.title: What the CA returns
docs.text:
Enroll, Poll, GetCert and GetCRL decide the answer through their return values:

Return Answer Certificates. A CRL for GetCRL CertRep SUCCESS with the certificates encrypted for the requester scepserver.ErrPending CertRep PENDING. Only Enroll and Poll may return it *scepserver.Failure CertRep FAILURE with Failure.Info as the failInfo. Failure.Err is logged and not sent *scepserver.Busy HTTP 503, with Busy.RetryAfter rounded up to whole seconds in a Retry-After header Any other error HTTP 500 with the body internal error. The error is logged

The handler finds these values with errors.Is and errors.As, so a wrapped *Failure still gives a FAILURE answer. A SUCCESS without certificates, an invalid failInfo and ErrPending from GetCert or GetCRL cannot be encoded and become HTTP 500. Unlike a FAILURE answer, an HTTP 500 does not end the transaction, so the client can send the request again later.

docs.title: The quickstart CA
docs.text:
The Getting started program implements the interface with one RSA key:

// quickstartCA issues a certificate for every PKCSReq that carries the challenge password and for
// every RenewalReq signed with a certificate it issued. It keeps nothing on disk.
type quickstartCA struct {
    cert     *x509.Certificate
    key      *rsa.PrivateKey
    password string
}

// newQuickstartCA creates a self-signed RSA CA that lives as long as the process.
func newQuickstartCA(password string) (*quickstartCA, error) {
    key, err := rsa.GenerateKey(rand.Reader, 2048)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    template := &x509.Certificate{
        SerialNumber:          randomSerial(),
        Subject:               pkix.Name{CommonName: "go-pki-scep quickstart CA"},
        NotBefore:             time.Now().Add(-time.Hour),
        NotAfter:              time.Now().Add(30 * 24 * time.Hour),
        IsCA:                  true,
        BasicConstraintsValid: true,
        // The CA key signs CertRep messages and decrypts requests, so it needs both usages.
        KeyUsage: x509.KeyUsageCertSign | x509.KeyUsageCRLSign |
            x509.KeyUsageDigitalSignature | x509.KeyUsageKeyEncipherment,
    }
    der, err := x509.CreateCertificate(rand.Reader, template, template, &key.PublicKey, key)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    cert, err := x509.ParseCertificate(der)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    return &quickstartCA{cert: cert, key: key, password: password}, nil
}

// CACertificates answers GetCACert with the CA certificate for any CA name.
func (ca *quickstartCA) CACertificates(context.Context, string) ([]*x509.Certificate, error) {
    return []*x509.Certificate{ca.cert}, nil
}

// Responder returns the CA identity when the request is encrypted for the CA certificate.
func (ca *quickstartCA) Responder(_ context.Context, recipient scep.IssuerAndSerial) (*scepserver.Responder, error) {
    if !bytes.Equal(recipient.Issuer, ca.cert.RawIssuer) || recipient.SerialNumber.Cmp(ca.cert.SerialNumber) != 0 {
        return nil, scepserver.ErrNotFound
    }
    // The RSA CA key signs the answers and, as a crypto.Decrypter, decrypts the requests.
    return &scepserver.Responder{SignerCertificate: ca.cert, SignerKey: ca.key}, nil
}

// Enroll authorizes a PKCSReq by its challenge password and a RenewalReq by its signer certificate.
func (ca *quickstartCA) Enroll(_ context.Context, req *scepserver.Request) ([]*x509.Certificate, error) {
    msg := req.Message
    switch msg.MessageType {
    case scep.PKCSReq:
        if subtle.ConstantTimeCompare([]byte(msg.ChallengePassword), []byte(ca.password)) != 1 {
            return nil, &scepserver.Failure{Info: scep.BadRequest, Err: errors.New("wrong challenge password")}
        }
    default:
        // A RenewalReq is signed with the certificate being renewed. A real CA also checks that the
        // certificate is not revoked and that the CSR asks for the same subject.
        signer := msg.SignerCertificate
        if err := signer.CheckSignatureFrom(ca.cert); err != nil {
            return nil, &scepserver.Failure{Info: scep.BadRequest, Err: fmt.Errorf("renewal signer: %w", err)}
        }
        // The handler refuses a signing-time outside the certificate validity, but that attribute is
        // optional and set by the signer, so check the current time too.
        if time.Now().After(signer.NotAfter) {
            return nil, &scepserver.Failure{Info: scep.BadRequest, Err: errors.New("renewal signer expired")}
        }
    }
    return ca.issue(msg.CSR)
}

// Poll refuses every CertPoll, because this CA never keeps a request pending.
func (ca *quickstartCA) Poll(context.Context, *scepserver.Request) ([]*x509.Certificate, error) {
    return nil, &scepserver.Failure{Info: scep.BadCertID, Err: errors.New("no pending request")}
}

// issue signs a one-day client certificate for the CSR key and returns it with the CA certificate.
func (ca *quickstartCA) issue(csr *x509.CertificateRequest) ([]*x509.Certificate, error) {
    der, err := x509.CreateCertificate(rand.Reader, &x509.Certificate{
        SerialNumber: randomSerial(),
        Subject:      csr.Subject,
        NotBefore:    time.Now().Add(-time.Minute),
        NotAfter:     time.Now().Add(24 * time.Hour),
        KeyUsage:     x509.KeyUsageDigitalSignature | x509.KeyUsageKeyEncipherment,
        ExtKeyUsage:  []x509.ExtKeyUsage{x509.ExtKeyUsageClientAuth},
    }, ca.cert, csr.PublicKey, ca.key)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    cert, err := x509.ParseCertificate(der)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    return []*x509.Certificate{cert, ca.cert}, nil
}

docs.title: Authorizing requests
docs.text:
The handler verifies the signature of a request, decrypts it and checks the CSR signature. It does not decide who may enroll. Enroll receives a *scepserver.Request with what it needs to decide:

Field Content Message.MessageType scep.PKCSReq, scep.RenewalReq or scep.UpdateReq Message.CSR The parsed CSR, whose signature the handler has checked Message.ChallengePassword The challengePassword attribute of the CSR. Empty without one Message.SignerCertificate The certificate that signed the request. The handler has checked that the requester holds its key and that the signing-time of the request, when present, falls within the certificate validity Message.TransactionID The transaction ID the client chose, which its CertPoll messages repeat Responder The identity the request was encrypted for, which tells a CA with several identities which one the client addressed HTTPRequest The client address, the headers and the TLS state

A PKCSReq is signed with a self-signed certificate, so the challenge password is usually the only proof the requester gives. Compare it in constant time with crypto/subtle, issue one password per device where you can and check that the CSR asks for a subject the password allows.

A RenewalReq is signed with the certificate being renewed. Check that your CA issued it, that it is valid now and not revoked and that the CSR asks for the same subject. The handler already refuses a request whose signing-time falls outside the validity of the signer certificate with HTTP 400. scepclient always sets that time, so a RenewalReq it signs with an expired certificate never reaches Enroll. Other clients may leave the attribute out or choose its value, so the CA checks the validity against the current time as well. In the examples on these pages myCA is your CA type and ca.cert, ca.key and helpers such as ca.revoked are its own state:

// authorizeRenewal accepts a RenewalReq signed with a valid certificate the CA issued for the
// subject the CSR asks for.
func (ca *myCA) authorizeRenewal(msg *scep.PKIMessage) error {
    signer := msg.SignerCertificate
    if err := signer.CheckSignatureFrom(ca.cert); err != nil {
        return &scepserver.Failure{Info: scep.BadRequest, Err: fmt.Errorf("renewal signer: %w", err)}
    }
    if now := time.Now(); now.Before(signer.NotBefore) || now.After(signer.NotAfter) {
        return &scepserver.Failure{Info: scep.BadRequest, Err: errors.New("renewal signer is not valid now")}
    }
    if ca.revoked(signer.SerialNumber) {
        return &scepserver.Failure{Info: scep.BadRequest, Err: errors.New("renewal signer is revoked")}
    }
    if !bytes.Equal(msg.CSR.RawSubject, signer.RawSubject) {
        return &scepserver.Failure{Info: scep.BadRequest, Err: errors.New("renewal asks for another subject")}
    }
    return nil
}

The default capabilities list Renewal, so clients may send a RenewalReq. A CA that does not renew this way can refuse it with a *Failure or replace the list through Options.Capabilities.

docs.title: Responders and RAs
docs.text:
Responder returns the identity that decrypts a request and signs its answer. The handler calls it with each recipient the pkiEnvelope names and uses the first identity it returns. Return scepserver.ErrNotFound for a recipient you do not hold. When no recipient matches, the handler answers HTTP 400.

The simplest responder is the CA itself. SignerKey then also decrypts, so it must implement crypto.Decrypter, as *rsa.PrivateKey does:

return &scepserver.Responder{SignerCertificate: ca.cert, SignerKey: ca.key}, nil

An RA answers for the CA with its own certificates, for example to keep the CA key offline or because the CA key is not RSA. With separate RA certificates for signing and encryption, return all of them from CACertificates and match the encryption certificate in Responder:

// CACertificates returns the CA certificate followed by the RA certificates.
func (ca *raCA) CACertificates(context.Context, string) ([]*x509.Certificate, error) {
    return []*x509.Certificate{ca.cert, ca.raSigner, ca.raEncrypter}, nil
}

// Responder returns the RA when the request is encrypted for its encryption certificate.
func (ca *raCA) Responder(_ context.Context, recipient scep.IssuerAndSerial) (*scepserver.Responder, error) {
    if !bytes.Equal(recipient.Issuer, ca.raEncrypter.RawIssuer) || recipient.SerialNumber.Cmp(ca.raEncrypter.SerialNumber) != 0 {
        return nil, scepserver.ErrNotFound
    }
    return &scepserver.Responder{
        SignerCertificate:    ca.raSigner,
        SignerKey:            ca.raSignerKey,
        DecrypterCertificate: ca.raEncrypter,
        DecrypterKey:         ca.raEncrypterKey,
        Certificates:         []*x509.Certificate{ca.cert},
    }, nil
}

Certificates travel in each CertRep next to the signer certificate, here the CA certificate. The client encrypts for RA certificates whose key usage allows key or data encipherment and accepts answers from RA certificates whose key usage allows digital signatures, as CA certificates and trust describes. Set the key usage of the RA certificates to match their role.

SCEP encrypts with RSA key transport, so the decrypter certificate and its key are RSA. The signer may be RSA or ECDSA. The keys are a crypto.Signer and a crypto.Decrypter, so they can stay in an HSM.

docs.title: Several CAs on one URL
docs.text:
GetCACert carries a message parameter that clients set to a CA name or leave empty. CACertificates receives it as name. Return scepserver.ErrNotFound for a name you do not serve, which the handler answers with HTTP 404.

PKIOperation requests carry no CA name. The handler finds the CA through the recipient of the pkiEnvelope, so give each CA its own decrypter certificate and read Request.Responder in Enroll to tell them apart.

docs.title: Mounting the handler
docs.text:
The handler serves every SCEP operation of one URL and picks the operation from the operation query parameter. Mount it at the path your clients are configured with:

handler, err := scepserver.NewHandler(ca, scepserver.Options{
    Logger: slog.New(slog.NewTextHandler(logs, nil)),
})
if err != nil {
    return nil, err
}
mux := http.NewServeMux()
mux.Handle("/scep", handler)

Serve it from an http.Server with timeouts, such as ReadHeaderTimeout. PKIOperation messages are limited to Options.MaxMessageBytes, 64 KiB by default. The handler does not rate limit clients, so add middleware for that.

docs.title: Optional operations
docs.text:
The handler checks whether the CA implements these interfaces and serves the matching operation only when it does.

Interface Operation Without the interface CertificateGetter GetCert, a PKIOperation FAILURE with badRequest CRLGetter GetCRL, a PKIOperation FAILURE with badRequest NextCAGetter GetNextCACert and the GetNextCACert capability HTTP 501 ChainGetter GetCACertChain HTTP 501

A CA that implements RefusalRecorder is told about the GetCert and GetCRL requests refused this way.

docs.title: GetCert
docs.text:
GetCert fetches a certificate by its issuer and serial number. ca.lookup stands for the certificate store of your CA.

// GetCert returns the certificate with the issuer and serial number the request names.
func (ca *myCA) GetCert(_ context.Context, req *scepserver.Request) ([]*x509.Certificate, error) {
    id := req.Message.CertificateID
    cert, ok := ca.lookup(id.SerialNumber)
    if !ok || !bytes.Equal(id.Issuer, ca.cert.RawSubject) {
        return nil, &scepserver.Failure{Info: scep.BadCertID, Err: errors.New("unknown certificate")}
    }
    return []*x509.Certificate{cert}, nil
}

Message.CertificateID holds the DER encoded issuer name and the serial number. Return the certificate first, optionally followed by its chain. The answer is encrypted for the certificate that signed the request, which is usually one the CA issued earlier. The handler does not check it, so decide in GetCert whether that signer may read the certificate.

docs.title: GetCRL
docs.text:
GetCRL names a certificate the same way and asks for the CRL that covers it. Return the DER encoded CRL. The handler sends it in a SUCCESS answer.

// GetCRL returns the current CRL of the CA.
func (ca *myCA) GetCRL(context.Context, *scepserver.Request) ([]byte, error) {
    return ca.currentCRL()
}

docs.title: GetNextCACert
docs.text:
Before a CA certificate expires, a CA can announce the certificate that replaces it. Clients fetch it with GetNextCACert and switch to it after the rollover.

// NextCACertificates announces the next CA certificate, signed by the current CA.
func (ca *myCA) NextCACertificates(_ context.Context, name string) ([]*x509.Certificate, *scepserver.Responder, error) {
    if ca.next == nil {
        return nil, nil, scepserver.ErrNotFound
    }
    return []*x509.Certificate{ca.next}, &scepserver.Responder{SignerCertificate: ca.cert, SignerKey: ca.key}, nil
}

The handler signs the certificates with the current responder, which clients already trust from GetCACert. The signature digest is Options.Digest. SHA-256 when it is zero. Return scepserver.ErrNotFound while no rollover is planned, which the handler answers with HTTP 404. A nil responder without an error is answered with HTTP 500.

When the CA implements NextCAGetter, the default capabilities list GetNextCACert.

docs.title: GetCACertChain
docs.text:
RFC 8894 does not define GetCACertChain, but some CAs serve it and their clients still send it. It returns the CA certificate followed by the certificates that issued it, up to the root.

// CACertificateChain returns the issuing CA certificate followed by its root.
func (ca *myCA) CACertificateChain(context.Context, string) ([]*x509.Certificate, error) {
    return []*x509.Certificate{ca.cert, ca.root}, nil
}

name is the message parameter, as for CACertificates. Return scepserver.ErrNotFound for a name you do not serve, which gives HTTP 404.

docs.title: Answer formats
docs.text: Operation Body Content type GetCACert with one certificate The DER certificate application/x-x509-ca-cert GetCACert with several certificates A certificate-only SignedData application/x-x509-ca-ra-cert GetCACertChain A certificate-only SignedData, also for one certificate application/x-x509-ca-ra-cert GetNextCACert A SignedData that the current responder signs and that carries only the next certificates application/x-x509-next-ca-cert GetCACaps One capability per line, each ending with a line feed text/plain; charset=utf-8 PKIOperation The CertRep pkiMessage application/x-pki-message

docs.title: Pending requests and throttling
docs.text: A CA does not have to decide at once. It can keep an enrollment pending until an operator or a backend approves it. It can also ask a client to come back later.

docs.title: Keeping a request pending
docs.text:
When Enroll returns scepserver.ErrPending, the handler answers PENDING. The client then sends CertPoll messages with the transaction ID of the enrollment. The handler passes each one to Poll. Poll answers like Enroll:

Poll returns Answer The issued certificate, optionally followed by its chain SUCCESS scepserver.ErrPending PENDING. The client polls again *scepserver.Failure, such as scep.BadCertID for an unknown transaction FAILURE

A CertPoll carries no CSR. It names the enrollment with these fields:

Field Content Message.TransactionID The transaction ID of the enrollment Message.PollRequest.Issuer The DER encoded name of the CA Message.PollRequest.Subject The DER encoded subject of the CSR Message.SignerCertificate The certificate that signed the CertPoll, which the answer is encrypted for

Keep the CSR with the transaction ID and check the subject when the client polls. The answer is encrypted for the certificate that signs the CertPoll, so also check that its key signed the enrollment. This CA keeps every authorized enrollment until approve is called. ca.authorize and ca.issue stand for the checks and the issuing of your CA:

// pendingRequest is an enrollment that waits for approval.
type pendingRequest struct {
    csr       *x509.CertificateRequest
    signerKey *rsa.PublicKey
    approved  bool
}

// Enroll keeps every authorized enrollment pending. The handler has checked that the signer key
// is RSA.
func (ca *pendingCA) Enroll(_ context.Context, req *scepserver.Request) ([]*x509.Certificate, error) {
    msg := req.Message
    if err := ca.authorize(msg); err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    ca.mu.Lock()
    defer ca.mu.Unlock()
    ca.pending[msg.TransactionID] = &pendingRequest{
        csr:       msg.CSR,
        signerKey: msg.SignerCertificate.PublicKey.(*rsa.PublicKey),
    }
    return nil, scepserver.ErrPending
}

// Poll issues the certificate of an approved enrollment.
func (ca *pendingCA) Poll(_ context.Context, req *scepserver.Request) ([]*x509.Certificate, error) {
    msg := req.Message
    ca.mu.Lock()
    p, ok := ca.pending[msg.TransactionID]
    approved := ok && p.approved
    ca.mu.Unlock()
    switch {
    case !ok || !bytes.Equal(msg.PollRequest.Subject, p.csr.RawSubject) || !p.signerKey.Equal(msg.SignerCertificate.PublicKey):
        return nil, &scepserver.Failure{Info: scep.BadCertID, Err: errors.New("unknown transaction")}
    case !approved:
        return nil, scepserver.ErrPending
    }
    return ca.issue(p.csr)
}

// approve lets the next CertPoll of the enrollment collect its certificate.
func (ca *pendingCA) approve(id scep.TransactionID) {
    ca.mu.Lock()
    defer ca.mu.Unlock()
    if p, ok := ca.pending[id]; ok {
        p.approved = true
    }
}

A real CA keeps pending requests in durable storage and removes them once they are issued, refused or expired.

docs.title: Transaction IDs
docs.text: The client chooses the transaction ID and repeats it in every CertPoll. Treat it as an opaque string. The parser accepts 1 to 256 characters. scepclient and scep.NewCSRRequest derive it from the CSR public key with scep.CSRTransactionID: the hex encoded leftmost 160 bits of the SHA-256 hash of the key, method 1 of RFC 7093. Other clients use other derivations, so do not recompute it on the server.

docs.title: Throttling with Busy
docs.text:
Return *scepserver.Busy to ask the client to send the same request again later, for example when it polls more often than the CA allows. Here p.lastPoll is a time.Time field that Poll sets on the pending request:

if time.Since(p.lastPoll) < time.Minute {
    return nil, &scepserver.Busy{RetryAfter: time.Minute - time.Since(p.lastPoll)}
}

The handler answers HTTP 503 with RetryAfter rounded up to whole seconds in a Retry-After header. It leaves the header out when RetryAfter is zero. It logs the deferral at the Info level as scep request deferred.

scepclient sends the same message again after the delay, as many times as Options.BusyRetries allows. A CA that returns *Busy must therefore not have acted on the request. To refuse it for good, return a *Failure instead.

*Busy throttles one transaction. Rate limits per client address or per device belong in HTTP middleware in front of the handler, which sees every request before it is parsed.

docs.title: Refusals and logging
docs.text: The handler refuses some requests itself, before or instead of calling the CA. This page lists those answers, the log records the handler writes and how a CA learns about refusals.

docs.title: HTTP refusals
docs.text:
These requests get an HTTP error and no CertRep. The body is a short reason and never contains the cause.

Request Status Body No operation parameter or an unknown operation 400 unknown SCEP operation GetCACaps, GetCACert, GetCACertChain or GetNextCACert with a method other than GET 405 with Allow: GET method not allowed PKIOperation with a method other than GET or POST 405 with Allow: GET, POST method not allowed GetCACert or GetCACertChain for a name the CA returns ErrNotFound for 404 unknown CA GetNextCACert while the CA returns ErrNotFound 404 no next CA certificate GetCACertChain or GetNextCACert when the CA lacks the interface 501 GetCACertChain is not supported or GetNextCACert is not supported PKIOperation POST with an empty body. GET without a valid base64 message 400 malformed PKIOperation request PKIOperation POST over MaxMessageBytes 413 malformed PKIOperation request PKIOperation GET with a message over MaxMessageBytes 414 malformed PKIOperation request A message that does not parse or whose signature does not verify 400 malformed or unverifiable pkiMessage A CertRep sent as a request 400 a CertRep is not a request A pkiEnvelope for which Responder returns ErrNotFound for every recipient 400 the pkiEnvelope is not addressed to this CA *Busy from the CA 503 with Retry-After busy, retry later Any other error from the CA or an answer that cannot be built 500 internal error

docs.title: FAILURE answers from the handler
docs.text:
These requests are answered with a FAILURE CertRep without reaching Enroll, Poll, GetCert or GetCRL:

Cause failInfo Failure.Err The signer certificate has no RSA key, so the answer could not be encrypted for it badAlg scepserver.ErrSignerNotRSA The pkiEnvelope uses a cipher Options.Decrypt does not accept or an unsupported algorithm badAlg The go-pkcs7 error, such as pkcs7.ErrContentEncryptionNotAllowed The pkiEnvelope does not decrypt with the responder key badMessageCheck Wraps pkcs7.ErrDecryptionFailed The decrypted content is not a valid CSR, CSR signature or query badRequest The parse error GetCert or GetCRL to a CA without CertificateGetter or CRLGetter badRequest GetCert is not supported or GetCRL is not supported

pkcs7.ErrDecryptionFailed does not say whether the key or the padding was wrong, so a sender cannot use the answer to probe the key.

docs.title: Recording refusals
docs.text:
A CA that implements scepserver.RefusalRecorder is called before each FAILURE answer in the table above. Use it for audit records or to count devices that send what the CA cannot accept:

// RecordRefusal writes an audit record for a request the handler refused on its own.
func (ca *myCA) RecordRefusal(ctx context.Context, req *scepserver.Request, failure *scepserver.Failure) {
    ca.audit.InfoContext(ctx, "scep request refused by the handler",
        "message_type", req.Message.MessageType.String(),
        "transaction_id", string(req.Message.TransactionID),
        "fail_info", failure.Info.String(),
        "signer_not_rsa", errors.Is(failure.Err, scepserver.ErrSignerNotRSA),
        "cause", failure.Err,
        "client", req.HTTPRequest.RemoteAddr)
}

The pkiEnvelope of the request may not be decrypted yet. Some refusals also concern messages without a CSR, such as GetCert. req.Message.CSRReqMessage, req.Message.PollRequest and req.Message.CertificateID can therefore be nil. req.Message.CSR is promoted from the embedded *CSRReqMessage, so reading it while that pointer is nil panics. Check the pointer first. The handler does not call RecordRefusal for the outcomes the CA returns itself or for the HTTP refusals.

docs.title: Log records
docs.text:
Options.Logger receives the records below. The default discards them.

Message Level Attributes Written for scep request answered Info message_type, transaction_id and status. For FAILURE also fail_info and cause when there is one Every CertRep, including FAILURE answers scep request deferred Info message_type, transaction_id, retry_after Every *Busy scep request refused Warn operation, status, reason, cause when there is one Every HTTP 404, 400, 413, 414 and 501 refusal except an unknown operation and a wrong method scep request failed Error operation, error Every HTTP 500

With slog.NewTextHandler, a refused request looks like this:

time=2026-11-03T15:06:54.157+01:00 level=INFO msg="scep request answered" message_type="PKCSReq (19)" transaction_id=B485DB38004DF987172810E833FB1BB48D72867B status="FAILURE (2)" fail_info="badRequest (2)" cause="wrong challenge password"

The cause is Failure.Err of the CA or of the handler. Keep secrets such as the challenge password out of it. The handler does not log the challenge password or the CSR.
